Pirates have set up a blockade near a hidden stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and are swarming over any passersby, which are mostly merchants and civilians.  Pirates tend to create these temporary blockades at ill-defended stargates, usually ones which have been set up by civilians and are not guarded by our forces.  But we still have an obligation to protect the citizens of {[location]agentConstellationID.name}.  Therefore I want you, {[character]player.name}, to fly to the stargate and eliminate the illegal blockade.

The merchants which own the gate you defended are very grateful for your assistance.  They told us to send you their best regards for a job well done.
I have cleared the blockade as you requested, {[character]agentID.name}.
Take care out there, {[character]player.name}.
I'll take care of these pests {[character]agentID.name}, just give me the coordinates and I'm good to go.
You're afraid of a few pirates?  Maybe I was wrong about you after all ...
Oh comon now, it isn't that hard.  Ah well, I'll find someone else to finish the job then.

Banidine and Scanners

We recently found a number of new mining fields in adjacent systems, and the usual assortment of pirate trash has come out of the woodwork to exploit it. We'll need them mined soon because even those thieving bastards have friends in places high enough to put the legal status of these sites in doubt. For some reason they've taken an interest even in Banidine, too, and we'll need to find out why; all my workers are busy with the more profitable fields, but I'm not taking any chances.

I'm uploading a bookmark to your People & Places databank; it shows the location of a Banidine mining operation. I need you to head out there and mine all the Banidine — should be 18,000 units, my foreman tells me. Once we've made an undisputed claim, we're free to mine there again without interference, and I'll provide you with a little something for your trouble.
Just say the word.
Here's the Banidine ore, {[character]agentID.name}. Seems like a waste of time to me, but hey, you're paying.
Listen, just leave the logistics of it all to me, okay? You mine, I plan, you mine some more. That's all you need to know.
I'm young, but I'm no rookie – I'll get your ore for you.
Thanks, youngster. You may prove yourself yet.
Yeah, I'm looking for work. Whatever you've got.
Here's your ore, {[character]agentID.name}.
Not bad, youngster. Not bad.

The easiest way to travel to a destination system quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group; once you have selected "Stargate" there, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in the mission details and choose "Set destination." You will notice that the next stargate along your route, both in space and in your Overview, is now yellow.

Next, right-click on the yellow stargate (in space or in the Overview) and select "Warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot, then sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

After you have completed the mission, if you have problems finding your way back to the agent, simply open the "People and Places" window from your NeoCom and check the Agents tab; the agent you are working for should be displayed there. Right-click on the appropriate agent and select "Set destination," then turn on your Autopilot to make your way back to the agent's system.
Helpful Hints

Damnation, they're sending them out younger and younger. Are you sure you're old enough to fly a starship? Oh, well, we have to play the hand we're dealt, and if you're the best I can get, I suppose you'll do.

We'll start simple, youngster. Banidine is normally all but worthless, so real miners don't usually bother with the stuff. Still, I've found a buyer who's willing to take whatever we can mine. So, get me 20,000 units of Banidine and I'll make it worth your while. It should be easy, even for a pup like you, but it will show me that you're serious.

There's an asteroid field near here that's lousy with the stuff – I've bookmarked it for you. Get back as soon as you can and I'll arrange a little bonus.
Twenty thousand Banidine? That doesn't sound too tough. Sure, I'm good for it.
Great, great. Maybe now I can get some work done.
You look preoccupied. Something I can help you with?
Here're your rocks.

Excellent! Maybe I'll finally get that raise.

Oh, uh, good job. Here's your payment.
Uhh... nah. Sorry. That's a little too pedestrian for me.
Dammit, don't make me mine this crap myself. I hate mining.

Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it into their mining packages when they produce ship scanners. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in the mission details and select "Add to Overview."
Helpful Hints

Well, maybe, yeah. Have you ever heard of Banidine? Doesn't matter, you have now. Anyway, my boss wants the stuff. Why? I have no idea — something to do with manufacturing cheaper parts, refrigeration units or something. I don't know. Point is, he's made it my job to get the ore. And now, if you're interested, I'm makin' it your job.

There's a few Banidine rocks out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enough for 20,000 units, the scouts tell me. Go out there, mine it, bring it back. Should be easy enough, right?
I can't wait around here forever. I'm getting someone else to mine the Banidine.
Your crippling indecisiveness
The mining isn't done... but I'm done with it.
Oh, for the love of... fine. Whatever. I'll get someone else to do it.
Look, if you can't point a beam at a few derelict Banidine rocks in a timely manner, I'm just gonna give the mission to someone else. Make sure you're ready to do some work next time you see me.
Your rampant laziness
Yeah, I'm game.
Get it quick. I don't like waiting.
You have anything for me?
Mine 18,000 units of Banidine at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring it to {[character]agentID.name}.
I've got your Banidine right here, pal.
Nice job. I'll remember this.
I don't work for crazy people.

Finding Banidine

Look, I need some… ah, building materials, but I've got a client who's a bit particular. He wants it special, from some asteroids that already destroyed a shuttle of his, I guess. He gave me a location; you just go there, mine all 18,000 units of the Banidine that's there, and bring it back. Now, you won't find this stuff anywhere else, so don't go looking to bring me back something similar and easier to come across — you try and rip me off on this, and I'll know. Got it? Alright.

So, you game?
I got no time for games. I'll find somebody who can get it done.
I'm done waiting
I'm done with this weird stuff. Banidine? It's worthless! So I get to wondering… who the hell wants this stuff, and for what? And I decide, maybe I ought not to do this, huh?
Thanks a bundle. I didn't pay ya to think. That's my job. Remember that next time.
I need this done yesterday. I found someone else who can do the job faster.
Too slow
I'll do what I can.
Excellent. Get out there as soon as you can.
I'm ready.

A huge asteroid has crashed into one of our stations. The station itself and most of the inhabitants are lost. This asteroid is particularly deadly in that it contains a huge quantity of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene so rescue crews can go in there and retrieve the survivors.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site. Mine it all and bring the ore back to me.
I have the ore onboard, {[character]agentID.name}.
Great work! I'll send in the rescue crews. I'm sure the families of the survivors will be delighted that you helped save their lives. And we might even find some way to use the Augumene.
I don't have time to save a few station-dwellers' lives.
Nice. Well, hopefully someone else will see the value in saving some civilian lives.

When mining for specific minerals, you can often use the Overview to help. Click the small white arrow beside the word “Overview”; from there, select “Load default,” and then “Mining.” Then, you can right-click any type of asteroid in your overview and select “Remove from Overview”; keep doing this until only the type you want is left in your overview.

Furthermore, if you plan to mine this type of ore regularly, you can click the Overview arrow again and select “Save current type selection as…”; type in whatever name seems appropriate. Now you can return to this setting anytime you want to simply by using the Overview arrow to select “Load (name).”
Helpful Hints

We need your help right away! We're calling on all ship commanders in this region. A huge asteroid has crashed into one of our stations. The station itself and most of the inhabitants are lost. This asteroid is particularly deadly in that it contains a huge quantity of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene so rescue crews can go in there and retrieve the survivors.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site. Mine it all and bring the ore back to me.
I don't have time to save a few station-dwellers' lives.
Hundreds more people will die now, thanks to you.
I understand. For the good of all, I'll clear out that Augumene.
Good. Get this done. I do not envy you your task.
What is it?

We've determined that the asteroid that collided with the station was composed of Augumene, which is particularly deadly in that it is a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene safely from a starship.

More than that, others may be coming for the Augumene. We can't recover all the sensitive material from the wreckage of the base in time, and a blockade would tip our hand. The only solution is to mine out the Augumene ourselves. We want you to go out and retrieve all of the Augumene from the site. And hurry.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site and then mine all the Augumene and bring the ore back to me.
I have done it. The remains of the station should now attract no unwanted attention.
Good work, {[character]player.name}. I wish we had not needed this to be done at all, but you did well.
I'm afraid I cannot do such a thing. It's… well, so many lives lost…
I understand. It's just this side of grave robbery. Still, desperate times, desperate measures, and all that.

Space stations are ideal research locations for most governments. Station crews can perform dangerous experiments that could endanger the civilians near a terrestrial base. Another advantage to the isolation of these stations is that they are harder for enemy factions to find, making espionage or outright destruction more difficult... usually.
Research Stations

Something terrible has happened. An asteroid has collided with a research station at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. There's no official death-toll yet, but it's expected to climb into the tens of thousands. Some of our brightest were there, working out the very technologies that would enable us to better defend our way of life from Gallente and Minmatar agressors. Now they're all gone....

I'm sorry. I lost myself there. We've determined that the asteroid that collided with the station was composed of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene safely from a starship.

More than that, others may be coming for the Augumene. We can't recover all the sensitive material from the wreckage of the station in time, and a blockade would tip our hand. The only solution is to mine out the Augumene ourselves. We want you to go out and retrieve all 3,600 units of Augumene from the site. And hurry. If we don't get that ore, looters might follow its signal and stumble on what's left of our base.
We cannot wait around forever. The task has gone to someone else.
This task is too urgent for your pace.
I can't do this anymore. It's too much.
Disappointing. I thought you seemed reliable.

You moved too slowly, {[character]player.name}. A recent recon shows that not only is the Augumene gone, but approximately 20 tons of material and data sheets are missing from the wreckage. We can only hope the thieves were merely scavengers.
Too late
I'll see what I can do.
Excellent. Don't waste any time.
I'm ready, I think.... Get started at what?

We've found a conglomeration of Augumene asteroids nearby. The ore's not much good to anyone due to the exorbitant cost of reprocessing, of course, but a couple of our scientists are interested in doing some research on such a rare substance. In any case, hopefully you've been around the block enough times that you can find the ore and bring it in.
The Augumene is here.
Not bad! Perhaps I was wrong about you.
Well, I'm sure I can find someone else to handle this.

We've found a conglomeration of Augumene asteroids nearby. In any case, hopefully you've been around the block enough times that you can find the ore and bring it in.

You think you're up to this? I've uploaded the location to your People & Places databank.
I didn't think you could handle it. Too bad I was right.
Most people don't go looking for Augumene: It's virtually worthless, so you simply won't find it on the market.
Helpful Hints
If it will help, I'll do this.
Thank you. We need to get this thing settled, and quick.
What is it? Have I done something wrong?

A commercial station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was destroyed in a freak accident. They're saying it was some sort of rogue asteroid, and it's fallen to us to analyze the thing. We're going to need all of it. Most of the asteroid is still at the site of the accident. It's a grim task, I know. But we need to do this if we're going to figure out how this happened.
I've retrieved all the ore samples.
Thanks. We'll get this to the boys in the lab immediately.
I'm not going to do this just to save your job.
You know, if you aren't part of the solution....

No, no, not at all—

Listen, it's just coming over the news channels now. There, see? A commercial station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was destroyed in a freak accident. They're saying it was some sort of rogue asteroid. Investigators are reporting over ten thousand confirmed dead so far. Naturally, people are demanding answers. The government wants answers, the media wants answers, the people want answers... you get the idea. And nobody seems to have any answers.

To put it simply, this shouldn't have happened. {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and its surrounding systems were cleared of rogue asteroids years ago, or so we thought. In fact, the station's position and orbit were chosen specifically to ensure its safety from collisions with celestial objects. If we don't find out how this asteroid got there, the finger pointing is going to start. Nobody's job will be safe once that starts happening.

It's fallen to us to analyze the asteroid. We're going to need all of it, {[character]player.name}. The asteroid is still at the site of the accident, though it's busted up some, I imagine.

It's a grim task, I know. But it's one we need to undertake if we're going to figure out how this terrible thing happened.
Never mind about the investigation. It's been handed off to someone else.
Investigation moved on
I can't continue on with this. Sorry.
Damn it, do you want me to lose my job?

About that asteroid collision: Don't worry about it. One of my coworkers just got sacked for it, and he was an idiot anyway. Looks like the whole thing is blowing over. Still, would have been nice to put solving this whole mess on my résumé.
Crisis averted
Sure, I think I can help you out.
Excellent! I'll get my lab ready.
Yeah, I'm looking for work.

I've just gotten word about a deposit of Augumene in this system. Now, we're not really sure what use we might make of it, but a number of our competitors seem to want it for research, so that means we need to move on it too. Go out to the bookmark I'll provide for you and mine every unit of the stuff you find there for us to study… before anyone else gets their hands on it.
I found your mystery rocks. Enjoy.
Wonderful! I'll get to work on this right away.
I'm not interested.
You're on their side, aren't you?

Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions — which more than negates any profit to be made from reprocessing the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.
About Augumene

I've just gotten word about a deposit of Augumene in this system. Now, we're not really sure what use we might make of it, but a number of our competitors seem to want it for research, so that means we need to move on it too. Go out to the bookmark I'll provide for you and mine every unit of the stuff you find there for us to study… before anyone else gets their hands on it.
I've got to get going on this research. I'll get someone else to find me some Augumene before it's too late to finish my dissertation.
I've got work to do.
I'm too busy to go looking for your mystery rocks. Sorry.
Oh, great! There goes my entire thesis. Four years of preliminary research, all brought to an end by you. Thanks.
I'm working under a deadline here. I'm never going to get my research finished now! I have to find a new topic for my dissertation because of your procrastination.
Thanks for nothing.
I can do that. Sure. Where to, again?
Excellent. Go quickly. I've uploaded the location to your NeoCom.
Heard…? I hear lots of things. Which thing are you talking about?
I've procured the Mercium for our cause.
{[character]player.name} , you are a credit to your people.
That sounds lame to me. No thanks.
Mercium Research

Ah, you haven't heard, apparently, or you'd know what I meant. Well, that's a relief. The fact is, we've gotten word of the location of a bunch of Mercium ore here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but we believe that our information has also been leaked to other factions — including the Gallenteans. It's vital that you collect all the Mercium: It cannot be allowed to fall into enemy hands.
We can wait no longer. I will seek out someone else to recover the Mercium before it is captured by our enemies.
Enemies abound
I'm not going to all that trouble over some worthless rocks. Sorry, but I quit.
If enemy factions get their hands on that Mercium, it's on your head, not mine.
You are too late. The Mercium is now in the hands of our enemies.
Mercium is lost
I understand. I'll get that ore in no time. No worries.
Go quickly, then. Time is precious!
Why? Work quickly on what? I'm in the dark here.

One of our sources obtained information on the whereabouts of a significant deposit of Mercium ore. It would be disastrous for our cause if this Mercium were to fall into Amarrian or Caldari hands. Unfortunately, we're certain that they already know about it, so as I said, we must work quickly.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
I got there first, I guess. Here's the ore.
Well done! Glad to have had you on board for this one.
I can't take that kind of pressure. Sorry.
If they find it first, it's on your head. Not mine.
Mercium Research

Oh, right. I was thinking I'd already sent you a com-chat about this. Heh. Sorry.

One of our sources obtained information on the whereabouts of a significant deposit of Mercium ore. It would be disastrous for our cause if this Mercium were to fall into Amarrian or Caldari hands. Unfortunately, we're certain that they already know about it, so as I said, we must work quickly.

Remember, they want that Mercium, so that means we need it more. Get it? You do whatever you have to to get this done quickly, alright?
I couldn't get the Mercium, and I'm not about to do it now. Sorry, but I quit.
If they find it first, it's on your head. Not mine.
Sounds like a good deal. I'm in.
Remember, move fast. Time's of the essence, huh?
What "thing" might that be?

Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
Here's your Mercium. So, where's my cut?

Here you go. Oh, this is gonna be just like hacking into that SCC station computer and making ISK for myself!

Uh, I mean, not that I've ever done that....
I'm not interested in getting caught in a four-way crossfire just to mine some rocks that might be worth something to someone at some point.
Not everybody's got what it takes. I knew that when I first looked at you.

I don't have this kinda time, {[character]player.name}. I gotta move on this Mercium before it's gone.
Going, going, gone
Selling to all four of the big empires? Uh... even I don't want to piss off that many people. Nah, I quit.
Don't worry, I'll find someone who's willing to make some decent ISK.
Somebody else already beat you to that Mercium, bonehead. Way to go.
Mercium's gone
If it needs to be done, it needs to be done. I'll get you the Lyavite.
Take care of yourself out there. The investigator I sent out is still having nightmares.
Whatever it is, you know I'm up for it.
I'm back from the ghost station, ore and all.
You made it back? You got the Lyavite okay? You didn't... see anything, did you? No? Okay. Good.
Something weird is going on here, and I'm not touching it. No thanks.
I'm not going to force you. But someone has to go.

Abandoned posts and stations aren't as uncommon as you might expect. Most are actually only half-built, victims of insufficient funding; often pirates or other drifters move in and patch holes just well enough to prevent decompression. Other times, the stations just aren't profitable or inhabitable, for any number of reasons, and it actually costs less to just leave the station floating there rather than to dismantle it.

But even then, there are usually records, people... something....
On Abandoned Stations

Well, we've got a bit of a weird one here. We've found an old mining post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But, the thing is, we can't find who used to own it: There are no records of its being built or even existing. It's simply empty. No sign of anyone left there, dead or otherwise. Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks — you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Anyway, near as we can tell, the miners were working on a large Lyavite deposit. They didn't finish, because there's still about 5,000 units of it at the site. Now, I know Lyavite isn't the most popular rock, but nobody just leaves that much ore lying around. And besides, the brains at the lab figure they can use the stuff for some of their research, so this opportunity is too good to pass up. That's where you come in. Warp in, mine the Lyavite, and warp out. It's that easy.

You are not going to believe this. Remember that abandoned mining post I told you about? The one with the Lyavite? It's gone. I don't mean someone else mined it, or it was raided or anything. It's just gone. We've sent five different scouts out there, and they all confirm that the location where the post used to be is just dead space.

Even the dust is gone.
Weird gets weirder
I've seen all sorts of crap as a pilot, and this is too creepy even for me. I'm out.
I'll not ask why. I'm sure you have your reasons.
Look, I know the mission sounded a bit off, but it needed to get done. My superiors are really putting the pressure on now, and I have to give this to someone else. I'm sorry.
Moving on
You're a little twisted. And I'm okay with that. Yeah, I'll get you your Augumene.
Excellent. Go get me some of that magnificent ore.
You seem happy. What is it?

I was talking to some blowhard in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} when his station was destroyed. So, I'm thinking raiders, right? But no, it's even better. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh!

It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me! I want you to go out there, and bring me back all of that Augumene.
Here's the Augumene. Where's my ISK?
Ah, it even feels like providence. And cold, hard kredits. Speaking of which, here's yours.
You seem entirely too happy with all this. And that troubles me. I'm going to decline, I'm afraid.
What? You don't like free ISK?

Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes very expensive safety precautions. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.
Augumene

I'm on the comm, talking to this blowhard I knew back from my days at the academy, right...? So he's going on and on about how his corporation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is going to make ISK hand over fist mining some rare ore, blah blah blah. Then all these alarms start going off on his end. And I'm thinking his stupid corp is getting raided or something. Then, all of a sudden, the wall behind him disappears and he's ripped away from the screen! The blowhard got spaced right in front of my eyes!

Now, here's the best part. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh! It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me!

So, anyway, I want you to go out there and bring me back all of that Augumene. Do that, and I'll have a nice reward here for you when your come back, alright?
I don't have time to wait for you to decide whether you like ISK or not. I'll get someone else to mine my lucky rock. So you can just get lost, okay?
My lucky rock
This is more than a little weird. I'm not mining this Augumene anymore.
Don't tell me you're scared of a little rock?
Great. You took just long enough for some other vultures to get all the Augumene. That rock was meant for me, but no, you had to prance around until it was too late. Thanks for nothing.
The Augumene is gone.
Prepare to change the world.
There's a rich deposit of Mercium in this system. Bring me 1,800 units and we might both end up rich.
Well, looks like the research guys have shot several holes in my Mercium reprocessing theory. Son of a… Well, you did your part, anyway: Here's your payment.
You simply have no vision.

Most people don't go looking for Mercium, as it doesn't do so well out on the open market. If you are having trouble finding it, you can right click the "Mercium" icon in your mission log and add it to your overview.
Mercium Mining

To be part of the future you need to help build it first. That's what I'm asking you to do.

There's a rare ore called Mercium, similar to Omber, but it's much more difficult to reprocess. Current methods render the ore unusable. It's maddening to no end. I think I might have solved the problem, though. I can't tell you my whole theory, but it's a variant on the standard electrolysis method used by planetside miners. All I need is some Mercium to try it on.

There's a rich deposit of Mercium in this system. Bring me 1,800 units and we might both end up rich.
I quit. Sorry, but I have better things to do with my time.
You simply have no vision.

The easiest way to travel to a destination station quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group. Once you have selected "stargate" in the Overview settings, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in your mission details and choose "set destination." You will notice that the applicable stargate in your Overview is now yellow, as well as the one in space that leads to the next system along your route.

Next, simply right-click on the yellow stargate in the Overview (or in space) and hit "warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot and simply sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

Once you have arrived in the correct star system, simply right-click anywhere in space. In the drop-down window that appears, your current mission information appears at the bottom. From there, select the "dock" option and your Autopilot will bring you into the station momentarily.

Once the slaves are delivered, return to your agent's home station (also available via the drop-down simply by right-clicking anywhere in space) to collect your reward.

It is important to the Empire that we get a shipment of elite slaves to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so that the workers there do not fall any further behind schedule.

Remember to move the slaves to your cargo hold before departure.
Helpful Hints

Excellent. As you know, it is the duty of every citizen to demonstrate his or her loyalty to the state from time to time. Though you are, at present, a small cog in the great machine of the Empire, you will find that even you have your place. We have a task for you that will help show your fitness to advance in our society and become a more significant part of that great machine.

It seems that the construction works at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are experiencing an unfortunate labor shortage, possibly brought on by their overly harsh personnel management methods. It is important to the Empire that we get them a shipment of elite slaves so that they do not fall any further behind schedule. Are you a loyal enough citizen to do this task and do it quickly?

I will upload a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to locate and reach your destination.
Well said, citizen. Good luck.
You have done well, citizen.
The Empire is disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
I am a loyal citizen. I will deliver the cargo.
The slaves have been successfully delivered, {[character]agentID.name}.
Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. I am seeking employment.

It just so happens that we're opening some new clubs over in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The problem is that the talent has gotten stranded here, and has to be over to the station for the grand opening. You probably know the rest. It's important that this be taken care of soon, so we're offering a substantial reward to anyone who wants to take the job.

Remember to move the dancers to your cargo hold before departure.
Helpful Hints

Hey, I'm glad you asked!

Here at Nugoeihuvi Corporation, we're all about pleasure. I'm sure you've seen our adverts — "If it's fun, it must be from Nugoeihuvi." And it just so happens that we're opening some new clubs over in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The problem is that the talent has gotten stranded here, and has to be over to the station for the grand opening. What talent you ask? Well, I mean the dancers, {[character]player.name}... Exotic dancing is an art form, you know, appreciated on the highest intellectual level. And we've got a bunch of dancers just standing around waiting for a ship to take 'em to their new home.

You probably know the rest. We need a fast, reliable pilot and a ship without any major mechanical problems. That brave and resourceful pilot needs to take these dancers to their destination so that they can get bringing in the high-rollers and thus earning their wages. It's important that this be taken care of soon, so we're offering a substantial reward to anyone who wants to take the job. You up to it, kid?
Good going. Now deliver those dancers, tiger! And try not to make too many stops along the way to… enjoy the merchandise, m'okay? Heh.
Thanks! We're counting the money already.
Okay, I guess I'll do it.
The dancers are dancing in your club as we speak, {[character]agentID.name}.
Hello, {[character]agentID.name}. Any work for a poor but honest young capsuleer?

You may have noticed all those marines hanging out in the loading bay. We've grabbed every available transport we can find, but there's still a few left behind who need to be transported to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Suffice to say, their presence is of vital importance to Federation efforts; if you're a loyal citizen, you'll take them to their destination.

Remember to move the marines to your cargo hold before departure.
Helpful Hints

Well, yes. Now, I can't say too much, but something's come up, and there's a great need for ground troops in a nearby system. You may have noticed all those marines hanging out in the loading bay. We've grabbed every available transport we can find, but there's still a few left behind who need to be transported to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Suffice to say, their presence is of vital importance to Federation efforts, and if you're a loyal citizen, you'll take them to their destination. And of course there's some extra pay in it for you. Will you help?
Thanks — the Federation won't soon forget this.
Good work, {[character]player.name}!
You've let down our glorious Federation, pilot.
I'll help you any way I can.
I've successfully transported the marines to their destination.
Hello. I hear you might have some work for a capsuleer like me?

On the loading dock is a shipment of weapons for our 412th Regiment, currently garrisoned at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Can you get it there for them?

Remember to move the High-Tech Small Arms to your cargo hold before departure.
Helpful Hints

These are dark days for our Republic, as you know. Our enemies threaten us on all sides, and our ancient traditions are in danger of dying out. We are a race of warriors, {[character]player.name}, and only through strength do we survive in a hostile universe. Our strength is in our warriors and in their weapons.

We believe that the cursed Amarrians are planning a major invasion, and we need to equip our warriors to repel their attacks on planetary environs. On the loading dock is a shipment of weapons for our 412th Regiment, currently garrisoned at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Can you get it there for them?
You are a true warrior, captain.
With the help of those weapons, our fighters will triumph. You have the Republic's gratitude, as well as my own, {[character]player.name}.
I will serve the Republic, as always.
The delivery is complete, {[character]agentID.name}.
I see a great deal of activity on the docks, {[character]agentID.name}. Is there anything I can help with?
One order of Azure Ice, coming up.
You and me, we're gonna go far.
Could be. Let me hear more, my friend.

There's a field of Azure Ice at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I want to sell it to some less-than-brilliant colonists. It's not as good as Blue Ice, but the they won't know the difference. Bring me back, oh, 20 blocks of it. I'll split the profit with you.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Azure Ice may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
Your "high-quality" Azure Ice is ready.
Excellent. I've already got your share of the money ready. This should keep their colony running just well enough so that they can make more orders.
Maybe I'll ruin the lives of unsuspecting colonists some other time, but not today.
Those colonists already ruined their lives. What's the harm in making some ISK off of that?

The open market doesn't bother with Azure Ice. Everyone and their grandmothers know it's not nearly as useful as Blue Ice. Planetary water ice has more demand. Any deal that gets you ISK for Azure Ice is a good sell. And if you ever get stuck with Azure Ice and no mission to turn it in... well, just be glad your docking bay has no volume limit.
Buyer Beware

Alright! You ever been out to some of those backwater colonies? You know the ones I mean. Barren wastelands of rocks and dust where some nut got the bright idea to try to build the agricultural community of tomorrow? Kind of place where the main export is despair? That kind of place?

Well, so happens I know of one that's just starting up. Poor bastards need some fuel. They're willing to pay good money, too. Now, I could sell them the good stuff, but seriously, these jokers wouldn't know good ice if it fell out of the sky and crushed their pet furrier.

There's a field of Azure Ice at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's not as good as Blue Ice, but the colonists won't know the difference. Bring me back about, oh, 20 blocks of it. I'll sell it to the colony goobers and cut you in. Sound good?

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Azure Ice may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
You moved too slow. Someone else got the sell. Not only that, but they got the right stuff for the job. How is anyone supposed to get repeat business if customers keep getting what they need?
Maybe ripping off colonists isn't the best use of my abilities.
As far as I'm concerned, there is never a better use of one's skills than exploiting the ignorant. Go figure.
You moved too slow. Someone else got the sell. Not only that, but they got the right stuff for the job. How is anyone supposed to get repeat business if customers keep getting what they need?
I'm on it. Back in a bit.
Excellent, {[character]player.name}. Thanks.
You know I do. What have you got?

We've located some asteroids that contain substantial amounts of Polygypsum — that's a comparatively rare mineral, and almost completely unknown in this system. Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with it. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. See you then.
It was awfully dull, but the reward should make some amends. Here's your ore.
You've earned your reward as far as I'm concerned, {[character]player.name}, that's for sure.
Hm. No, I think I'm going to go, oh… watch some paint dry, actually. Thanks for the offer, though.
I see. Well, I guess I can find someone else willing to make an easy few ISK.
Mining Polygypsum
Sure, I'll see what I can do.
Don't waste any time. These guys are waiting for their ore.
We do? Or I do? Either way, I'm ready. What's up?

We need a big shipment of Geodite crystals for a client of ours, some gemology lab. These gemologists figure they might be able to get some decent stones out of it and make a bit of profit that way. Whatever. They want to pay for it, so it's all good by me. And you'll get your cut, don't worry.

Geodite takes up a lot of room: You're going to need a big cargo hold, or you'll have to make several trips.
Here's your load of Geodite.
Nice work. I'll keep you in mind when something else comes up.
That's one boring scenario you've worked out there, my friend. I think I'm gonna pass.
Man, I hope I can find someone else to handle this.

Geodite ore is pretty much worthless because of the poor-quality Nocxium it produces; one is far better off to look for Crokite instead... although that's no easy job. In any case, you won't find Geodite on the market anywhere.

If you're having trouble finding the Geodite at the mission location, you can right-click the "Geodite" icon in the mission's details and select "Add to Overview."
Geodite Ore

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has an unusual request for the right miner. We need a big shipment of Geodite crystals for a client of ours, some gemology lab. Maybe you've heard of Geodite, but if not, it'd be no surprise — the stuff's pretty much worthless. But these gemologists figure they might be able to get some decent stones out of it and make a bit of profit that way. Whatever. They want to pay for it, so it's all good by me. And you'll get your cut, don't worry.

Anyway, if you're interested, I'll send the coordinates over to your ship's NeoCom — the field's in this system.
Hm. This is a pretty boring scenario you've worked out here, my friend. I think I'm gonna cut out.
Maybe next time. Once again progress grinds to a halt.
You know I'm never one to shy away from my patriotic duty.
Be quick about it. We don't want to let anyone else beat us to that Oeryl.
Hear what, {[character]agentID.name}?

It's the sound of war! It's been too long since the blaring of military marches has been heard, the stockpiling of weapons undertaken, the murderous idealism of a young generation inveigled. And to me it all seems like the clinking of ISK.

War is one of the biggest boons to business you could hope for. It's a hungry giant that will eat anything you can throw at it. And the thing is, if you don't feed it, it will just eat you…. But if you feed it well? Oh, the rewards. Public recognition, sure, but the contracts, the contracts, {[character]player.name}! That's where the real ISK is. And we're going to get those contracts. Oh, yes. But first we need minerals.

Right now, it seems the giant on our doorstep wants Oeryl, and we're going to give it to him. There's a deposit out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Bring back all 5,600 units of the stuff and I'll make sure you get your share of the reward.

Here's the Oeryl. Uh, for the war effort.
Good work, {[character]player.name}. Just remember, you're not a profiteer — you're securing the financial stability of the homefront.
I'm not comfortable with the moral implications of this job.
I knew you were one of those spineless sympathizers.

It has been nearly a century since the Caldari-Gallente War, the last major war between any of the Great Empires, came to a close. Though skirmishes have broken out here and there, the distractions of the ever-expanding "lawless" space and the efforts of organizations such as CONCORD have helped maintain an uneasy peace. But no peace lasts forever.
Of Peace and Preparation
While you were puttering around, deciding whether you were going to do the Oeryl job, the government went and got its ore from another seller. Nice effort. Or rather, lack thereof.
Oeryl contract lost
I can't continue doing this. Sorry, but I quit.
Do you want the enemy to win? Do you?
In the time it took you to fail this mission, nearly 250 brave pilots lost their lives. You also failed to make a load of money. You need to do better.
Time is money. Blood money.
Yeah, okay, I'll get your rock…
Well, get going then! I need that rock!
Hm. Depends on the job…

I hear there's some Green Arisite that a bunch of people are looking to get their hands on. Now, I don't know why they want it, but if they want it, I want it. You may have to hunt for it a bit; I hear the belt's got a lot of big broken-up old asteroids floating around. Might be a little creepy, but it shouldn't do you any harm, and I want that damn rock!
I got there first! Here's your stupid green rock.
Hah! Who's the stupid one?! Now I can sell it for a fortune to those other jerks!
I think I'll pass. Also, you might want to cool off a bit.
If I cooled off, I wouldn't have a business. Now move along.
Green Arisite

Look, I hear there's some Green Arisite that a bunch of people are looking to get their hands on. Now, I don't know why they want it, but if they want it, I want it.

You may have to hunt for it a bit; I hear the belt's got a lot of big broken-up old asteroids floating around. Might be a little creepy, but it shouldn't do you any harm, and I want that damn rock!

Go get it before those other bastards get their grubby hands on it!
On second thought? I'm out of here. And I think you're a little crazy.
Yeah — like a fox! Suit yourself, it's your loss.
If the pay is good, I'm there.
Indeed. And paid you will be.
Why is that? You got something for me?

Demand for minerals is skyrocketing. Which is good for us. More demand means more profit.

To fill that demand, though, we're having to turn to some unorthodox ores: Green Arisite, for instance. I know of a large field that's full of the stuff. If you can get it for me, I'll make sure you're reimbursed. We just may be able to make some use of it, with the right tech. Who knows?
Your Green Arisite. But I think you're gonna lose your shirt on this one…
Good job. Nice working with you
Not today, sorry. Uh, my cousin just asked for help moving some furniture…
I guess I'll find someone who likes ISK, then.

Green Arisite is relatively worthless because of the high costs of reprocessing; one is far better off mining Gneiss instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Arisite at the mission location, just right-click the "Green Arisite" icon in  this mission's details in your Opportunities interface and select "Add to Overview."
Green Arisite

I do. And it's going to be a big haul.

Demand for minerals is skyrocketing. All the big empires are stockpiling for the coming fight. Oh, come on, you've seen the signs! Ships, rockets, drones, fortifications — all these things take material. The skirmishes out in 0.0 aren't lessening the demand any, either. Which is good for us. More demand means more profit.

To fill that demand, we're having to turn to some unorthodox ores. Green Arisite, for instance. I know of a large field that's full of the stuff. If you can get it for me, I'll make sure you're reimbursed. We just may be able to make some use of it, with the right tech. Who knows?

Too. Many. Rocks. Uhhhh…

I quit.
What kind of miner are you?
It just so happens I am trained in Gas Harvesters. I'll do it.
Thank you. Get back as quickly as you can.
What's up? Happy to help.

I need pain medications badly. I can't just wait for the next delivery. I need to produce my own drugs. For that I'm going to need Gamboge Cytoserocin. I heard a smuggler say there was a pocket at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go there, and bring back everything you can. I'll try to make it worth your while.

You need to fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission.
Here's your gas. Do some good with it.
More good will come from this than you know.
I'm afraid I cannot do this.
Okay, that's fine. It's better that you're upfront with these things than not.

Although the compounds that are popularly called "boosters" are illegal in empire space, other legal derivatives of gas cloud materials are used in the medical community. These medicinal drugs are highly controlled, but are often the difference between life and death for many citizens.
Medicinal Drugs

The government says we're prepared for war. You wouldn't know it by looking at our wounded. Space makes everything worse. Just look through the medical bay. Second-degree burns and frostbite are both alarmingly common, and are usually in conjunction with other serious injuries.

I need pain medications badly. I can't just wait for the next delivery. I need to produce my own drugs. For that I'm going to need Gamboge Cytoserocin. I heard a smuggler say there was a pocket at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go there, and bring back everything you can. I'll try to make it worth your while.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.
Take this soil to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so our science weenies can figure out how to grow stuff for us to eat. No lollygagging.

Some egg-heads we hired've been analyzing a nearby planet for "sustainable food resource population." Heh, yeah. Anyway, looks like our plans to terraform it are moving forward.

Now, a big part of this project is good, fertile soil. Yeah, soil. Think about it.

But before the project can move full ahead, we need someone to transport sort of a small amount of the stuff to test out the growing conditions. And that means someone with a big enough cargo hold and a desire to make a bit of ISK for the effort.

So, what do you think? Are you interested?

Hey, don't give me that look. It might be mud, but it's important mud!

Oh, just get going.
Alright, alright, wiseguy. Here's your ISK. Pleasure doin' business, and all that.
Uhh, well… yeah, sure, I guess. I mean, ISK is ISK, right?
Okay, your name is mud. Or, rather, your mud is delivered. So pay up.
Dirt transporting, huh? You do realize that I'm a capsuleer, right? Not some common industrial pilot?! Thanks, but no thanks.
Uh, it's "pod pilot." So what's going on?
Take this soil to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so our science weenies can figure out how to grow stuff for us to eat. No lollygagging.

Some egg-heads we hired have been analyzing a nearby planet for "sustainable food resource population." Heh, yeah. Give a nerd an edumucation, and he thinks he gets to make up all sorts of dumb names for stuff. Anyway, looks like the plans to terraform the planet are moving forward.

Now, a big part of this project is good, fertile soil. But before the project can move full ahead, we need someone to take a small amount to their lab to test out the growing conditions. And naturally, I can't think of anyone I'd rather pay for such an easy job but you.

So, what do you think? Are you interested?

Hey, don't gimme that look. It might be mud, but it's important mud!

Oh, just get going.
Alright, alright, wiseguy. Enough with the wit, already. Pleasure doin' business as usual.

The easiest way to travel to a destination station quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group. Once you have selected "stargate" in the Overview settings, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in the mission details in your Opportunities interface and choose "set destination." You will notice that the applicable stargate in your Overview is now yellow, as well as the one in space that leads to the next system along your route.

Next, simply right-click on the yellow stargate in the Overview (or in space) and hit "warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot and simply sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

Once you have arrived in the correct star system, simply right-click anywhere in space. In the drop-down window that appears, your current mission information appears at the bottom. From there, select the "dock" option and your Autopilot will bring you into the station momentarily.

Once the weapons are delivered, return to your agent's home station (also available via the drop-down simply by right-clicking anywhere in space) to collect your reward.

There are few who can deny the majestic beauty of an ice field: the slowly rotating towers of glistening blue-green ice set against the colder backdrop of the stars can give even the most jaded pilot pause. Yet such beauty hides a darker truth: if you are not prepared, an ice field can quickly become your very own sparkling graveyard.

While some ice fields can be found in Empire space, the rarer– and more profitable– ice ores are found in 0.0 space. As always, low sec can promise more ISK– or it can promise the dubious thrill of seeing your ship pounded into dust by eager pirates. Far too many inexperienced pilots have seen their mining barges blown apart-- with the hours and ISK needed to outfit them-- now so much vapor floating around their blinking pod.

Yet for most, the lure of the ice fields is too much to resist. With the sure promise of such treasures as Strontium Clathrates and Liquid Ozone, to name a few, the dangers of low sec will be dared. And even if it all ends in a fiery explosion, pilots can still enjoy the way their ship's destruction makes the ice sparkle all that more beautifully, if only for a few, rare seconds.

Our security and military ground forces have been experiencing a slow but steady increase in the numbers and severity of injuries suffered during a wide range of armed conflicts. A recent study by Amarr military scientists has determined that the primary cause of this has been a failure to adequately improve the lightweight body armor worn by millions of our soldiers, Marines, police, and other fighting forces. As fate would have it, one of our intelligence units has obtained what they claim to be a revolutionary new fabric that could provide fifty percent better protection across the board in all types of engagements. We need you to deliver this very sensitive cargo to a station we designate.

Thank you for coming, pilot. As you know, the Amarr Empire is in a constant state of conflict. Our enemies have included organized criminal gangs, drug traffickers, terrorists of every conceivable motivation, pirates, unpacified slave populations, and even the occasional low level skirmish against our fair-weather friends, the Caldari, Gallente, and, lest we forget, the Minmatar. This requires the Empire to always remain vigilant to any situations that may call for the use of force on levels ranging from simple urban pacification to outright military combat. What you do not know is that a high-level internal Empire report has revealed that our casualty levels have been steadily increasing over the last several years, often requiring evacuation to more robust – and already overburdened – medical facilities.

In the “recommendations” section of this report, the researchers concluded that the single most identifiable cause of these excessive casualties is a systemic problem with our lightweight body armor. This armor is standard issue for millions of police and security personnel, as well as our military reconnaissance units. Unless a drastic improvement in the quality and durability of this body armor can be found, we will continue to suffer the consequences.

This morning I received a priority communication from an Amarr Intelligence Officer claiming that his team had just “obtained” a revolutionary new fabric that, if properly processed, could literally double the strength of our existing armor. I know this officer only by reputation, and it is best not to pry any further into how his team came across this “miracle cloth.” Nonetheless, we have been advised that they will arrive at this station within moments to transfer the fabric here for transshipment to a more secure facility.

So, pilot, will you transport this prototype body armor fabric to the station facility we designate?
Lightweight Body Armor

Quitting mid-mission is not something I expected from you. Now I am going to have to answer to the intelligence team. Oh, and don't expect any further jobs from me until your failure here has been long forgotten. Damn… I need a stress pill….

I must say I am disappointed in your decision to turn down this mission. I vouched for you personally, given what I have seen in your files about your excellent mission completion record. I will not soon forget your refusal.

Lightweight body armor is a common and often required element of any police or security forces' operational gear. Modern armor of this type can stop most projectile, laser, and other light weapon fire. However, as small arms weaponry continued to evolve with regard to the amount of damage it can inflict, so to must the defensive technologies designed to maintain parity with these weapons. On rare occasions, a corporation, military laboratory, or other entity will produce a light body armor system that represents nothing short of a generational leap in design and protection. The multilayered fabrics used in these latter applications are usually amongst the most highly guarded secrets of any civilization, for many reasons. The most advanced of these contain nanotechnology which also can change color and density depending on ambient conditions and/or input from the wearer.

Outstanding, pilot. You were even a bit ahead of schedule. Our offloading team is en route to your ship, and the Intel guards will stay with the shipment until that has been completed. I will keep your name in my “go to” list should any more missions come up in the future.
Thank you for the update pilot, but no need to contact me until you arrive. The Intel security team on your ship is keeping me quite well informed.

A small, platoon-sized Caldari special operation team is in hiding on a Gallente planet and in danger of being captured or killed. They are low on water, food, weapons, and other equipment and will not last long unless they are extracted. We have a rescue standing by; however, we need you to deliver the required materials to their station so that they can then proceed with this critical rescue mission.

One of our Caldari Navy Special Forces units conducting clandestine reconnaissance of a contested ocean planet – a Gallente-claimed planet, by the way, with extremely rare seabed minerals – sent an emergency burst communication to the covert ops ship in orbit above the planet, requesting immediate extraction. This signal was, in turn, transmitted to the classified comms center here on this station. When we attempted to contact both the team and the ship, however, we received no response. Our immediate reaction was to divert one of our long range Crow-class interceptors, which was in the region on an unrelated mission, to investigate. Soon after its arrival, its sensors confirmed that the covert ops ship had been destroyed.

There is nothing we can do for our lost covops ship; however, this series of events has left the Special Forces team alone and without a means to evacuate the planet. Even worse was a fragment from the original communication indicating that the team was on the run and low on food, water, weapons, and ammunition. They have taken refuge in a disused ocean mining facility, though it is doubtful that they will stay hidden for long. There simply aren't many places to hide on that planet, given the fact that it is mostly covered by massive oceans, with very little land mass. It will not take long for the Gallente to track down our team and either kill them or, worse, capture them for interrogation.

The good news in all this is that we have an extraction team in place, along with a shuttle-equipped vessel to deliver them to the planet. However, given the immediacy of this mission, they had to leave their original base without much of their usual equipment and weaponry. This is where you come in. We need you to transport several containers of highly specialized small arms and related equipment to the station at which the extraction team is currently located. Once you drop off this cargo, the team will gear-up and shuttle down to the planet to rescue the stranded team.

So, pilot, what is it gonna be? Will you help us?
Do not contact us until you have completed this shipment. There is simply no time for idle chatter, not to mention the likelihood that the enemy is almost certainly listening in.

We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our military personnel at great risk. It is doubtful that we will be able to find anyone else to get this critical shipment to the station in time.
Your refusal to accept this mission will almost certainly result in the loss of this Special Forces team, not to mention placing the now-dangerously unequipped extraction team at great risk.
Thank you for accepting this important, time-sensitive mission. You have been given priority clearance for station undock, so please leave as soon as possible.

Due to a recent series of inspections by the regional mine monitoring commission, we have found it necessary to purchase a large quantity of the latest generation of environmentally-friendly drills and related equipment.

In order to avoid financial penalties and the possible loss of our mining rights, that company must get these quite expensive new drills into the hands of the miners as soon as possible. If you can deliver this cargo to the station that serves as our logistical hub for this system, they can then have their own pilots transship them to the required planetary mining locations.

Let me start at the beginning. As you have probably seen on the news channels, a prominent Caldari mining company is in the middle of a very nasty battle for economic survival with a new, up-and-coming mining company from within the same large conglomerate. Both of these companies specialize in the extraction of ores from some of the more inhospitable and dangerous locations in this and several adjoining systems. While this can be hazardous with regard to men and equipment, the profit potential from these largely untapped ore reserves can be quite significant, which brings me to our current predicament.

As you may know, the specialized manual labor required for some of these mines can be significant in terms of numbers. Well, the Mining Health and Safety Commission, or MHSC, for this region recently conducted a survey of the first company's operations, and found that their mining practices at certain locations may have resulted in excessive pollution, then further alleged a corresponding link to long-term miner health problems. The company has loudly complained that this is a ridiculous witch hunt brought about by their new competitor, which happens to have several “friends” on the commission. While they work to ensure they are equally “represented” on that commission, the recent finding has mandated that they immediately improve worker conditions and reduce pollution or risk losing their mining rights. To remedy this problem, they recently purchased a large number of the latest environmentally-friendly – and obscenely expensive – manportable drills, which seems to have assuaged the MHSC for the moment. They do, however, have a deadline for actually putting these new drills into the hands of the miners, which brings us to the reason I contacted you.

We need you to deliver a rather large shipment of drills and other related equipment to a station that serves as a central service hub. From there, logistics pilots will deliver this and other items to the various mines in the system. Will you take on this important job?

We are shocked to hear that you have chosen to quit this job in the middle of the contract. We will now have to pay another pilot double to pick up where you left off. You should have let us know from the outset that you could not take on this important job. Hopefully, we will never have to rely on you again.
Well, I must say we are quite disappointed that you would turn down this very easy contract. We shall find another pilot and move your name to the bottom of our list. Don't call us, we'll call you.

I certainly do appreciate your help, pilot. Hopefully, if we can get these drills into the hands of the miners in short order, the company should be able to retain its mining rights and return to profitability.
You seem to be on schedule and we look forward to the prompt delivery of the equipment to the designated station. Contact us through the usual channels after you have offloaded this gear.

Job well done. Our logistics teams are loading your shipment into their transport vessels as we speak, and we should have the drills and equipment in place shortly. We will definitely contact you again, should we require your services.

There has been an uprising at one of our slave Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRCs, near a rather large ore mine. The slaves are almost wholly Minmatar, so we cannot afford to have this incident continue for even one more day. The longer it goes on, the greater the chances that some reporter or news agency will get wind of this and splash the story all over the region. Given that the Minmatar Republic may feel compelled to take action to aid their brethren, this can only lead to dire consequences. That, of course, is unacceptable. We do have a plan in place, however, that should end this uprising before it has a chance to truly take root. We need you to transport a large contingent of Riot Interdiction Team (RIT) personnel to a designated station. From there the assembled security teams will join up and embark a small fleet of frigates and cruisers to race to the prison, where they will use all necessary force to terminate this uprising before it gets completely out of control.
Bah – I should have known you wouldn't help us. I could tell when I first met you that you were beyond salvation.
Good job, pilot. Please make all possible haste to the station as the other teams are waiting on you. The assault phase will begin after you deliver the RIT personnel and their equipment.

The Amarr Empire, realizing many centuries ago that it could not simply work slaves to the point of death, instituted a number of improvements to worker conditions in an effort to prolong the usable lifespan of its slaves. These changes were not universal across the Empire, due in large part to the Empress's unwillingness to create what might have amounted to significant friction between slave -based companies. Therefore, these decisions were largely left to the Five Heirs and their subordinate regional offices. Thus, we can state here that history has shown a lack of consistent application of these worker improvement programs across the Empire. Those Amarr systems that have chosen to incorporate these adaptations have, however, consistently derived greater revenues due to these enhanced and ongoing pacification efforts.

These shortcomings led directly to the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers (LRC). An LRC is designed much like a multilevel prison, with facilities for low, medium, and high risk inmates. The inmates are those slaves who consistently exhibit defiance or even outright hostility towards the managerial staff at the mine, construction site, or other location to which they are assigned as slave labor. Once we have identified these persons they are immediately removed from their job site and taken to the nearest LRC for corrective behavioral conditioning. This conditioning can include a wide variety of attitude modification methodologies, from intensive drug assisted counseling, to religious indoctrination, and from advanced torture techniques and a concurrent system of rewards - the so-called “carrot and stick approach” - and any number of programs in between. In this way, we break the individual slave's will so that he may be returned to the workforce as a docile and useful component in the labor pool.

Bless the Empress – I am very glad to hear you've decided to help. The RIT personnel will meet you in the hangar bay shortly.  Please feel free to take any of our religious literature with you for your enlightenment during the flight.
You soulless coward! Without the men you agreed to deliver our assault on the prison will undoubtedly lead to unnecessary casualties on all sides.
Amarr Labor Reeducation Centers (LRC)

Following a string of suicide terrorist attacks yesterday, we managed to capture a high ranking member of their organization. Interrogations have revealed, however, that a devastating viral weapon, based on nanotechnology, is already in place and primed for release. We need you to deliver the only known countermeasure to this agent, manportable electromagnetic weapons. If we are successful, these weapons could eradicate the virus before it has a chance to spread and infect the entire station.
Pilot, there is simply no time to discuss this any further. Deliver the cargo to the station immediately, before that horrible weapon kills thousands of innocent men, women, and children.

Last night, a strike team of suicide terrorists from the Anti-Corporatist Revolutionary Front, or ACRF, struck at more than twenty Caldari offices and stations throughout the region. During one of these attacks a terrorist was captured with a well-shielded, improvised nuclear device hidden in his rucksack. Obviously this event represents an entirely new level of threat from the ACRF, now that they have proven themselves willing to carry out such a horrendous and indiscriminate mass casualty attack.

The only upside to this is that the terrorist has turned out to be the most notorious operative of the ACRF, a woman known as Commander Rachendia. Having her in custody has offered us an opportunity to gain information related to her group's future plans to strike at the Caldari State. During one of the more aggressive interrogations, she disclosed information about a pending attack against one of our nearby stations. The nature of the attack is not entirely clear; however, we know with certainty that it involves the surreptitious introduction of a viral agent into the life support and air circulation systems.

Our initial searches for these hidden canisters at that station have, so far, been fruitless – with the exception of one small aerosol-type canister. A preliminary test revealed that these viral weapons appear to be based on a self-replicating nanotechnology. Once released from stasis in their container, they seek out and consume human tissue, and leaving behind little more than dust. Our medical scientists have calculated that just one container, released into the central air processing vents, could result in the deaths of all human life aboard a medium-sized station within no more than four hours. The only good news is that these nanos are programmed to self-terminate within 12 hours. Of course, this would be far more time than would be necessary to kill everyone aboard all but the largest of stations.

Your role in this desperate situation is to deliver a cargo of electromagnetic weapons, modified to emit a short-range pulse that will literally "fry" any nanos within its range. So, we are asking: will you deliver these containers to the station immediately? Thousands of lives may depend on your answer.

We had placed all our hope in you completing this mission. It's too late now to find another pilot and another ship. I fear many thousands of lives may be lost due to what can only be your cowardice. Obviously, you are not a man of your word, and we won't forget that.

Your bravery and skillful piloting without question, saved the lives of untold numbers of innocent people. We will definitely move your name to the top of our list for any future time-sensitive missions!
We're very glad to hear you are willing to take on this important mission. If we can get these EM devices to the station in time, I know we can save many innocent lives.

We are all terribly disappointed in your refusal to transport these electromagnetic weapons to the station. We shall now have to find another pilot and another ship, and I fear even then we will be too late. I doubt you will be sleeping very well after you see what may become of that station.

Terrorists, working with criminal scientists, have developed a strain of viral weaponry that is based on nanotechnology. When combined, the "hive mind" of the viral strain works to seek out human tissue at which point the microscopic nanos begin to quickly disassemble the tissue, leading to a slow and painful death. Research into electromagnetic pulses has provided some promising leads with regard to countermeasures, but these have not yet been field tested.
Nanotechnology-based Viral Weapons

The Imperial Navy recently made a final attempt to scour the battlefield graveyard of The Battle of Vak-Atioth. This battle pitted our brave Navy against the Jovian enemy; however, due to a number of unforeseeable factors, we did not emerge victorious. The graveyard itself has been picked over for decades by scavengers and others seeking some quick isk. The Amarr ships sent to perform this duty were attacked by pirates, and only one ship eventually returned. But when it did, it brought with it a valuable icon of Amarr military history: a selection of data chips holding recordings of a small part of that legendary battle. We need these chips delivered to a distant station for proper cleaning and processing.

As you almost certainly know, many decades ago our Grand Fleet met the hated Jovians on the field of battle in a system known as Vak-Atioth. Most unfortunately, our fleet was destroyed by the technologically superior Jovian ships and their advanced weaponry, marking one of the darkest moments in our history. Still, we learned much from this encounter, and the lessons learned there continue to benefit our military to this day, which brings us to why I called you here.

Several days ago, Imperial naval intelligence mounted a highly classified effort to revisit the Vak-Atioth system, now known simply as Atioth, to conduct a final intensive search for any remaining debris that might provide some insight into the tactics and weapons used by the Jovians. Needless to say, this once-massive floating graveyard has long since been picked over by not only our own salvage fleets, but by scavengers and opportunists alike. All has not been lost, however.

Much to our surprise, the Anathema covert ops ships sent to scan this system returned with a damaged but still readable supply of TIL-1A Nexus Chips. A preliminary review of the information they contain reveals only a portion of the great battle. We are hoping, however, that a more thorough analysis of these chips will reveal some insight into Jovian tactics and technology. If nothing else, they provide a very rare first-hand accounting of the battle which will add greatly to our historical archives and, when displayed at one of our leading military academies, will provide a stirring motivational icon for future generations of brave Imperial naval warriors.

Now that you understand the importance of these chips to the Empire, I must ask: will you transport this invaluable cargo to the designated station?

Many decades ago, a large portion of the Imperial Grand Navy met the Jovians in combat at what today is referred to as The Battle of Vak-Atioth. It was our intention in opening that battle with the as-yet untested Jovians to destroy their fleet utterly, thus forcing their subjugation, as we had done with so many enemies in the past. Without going into great detail, the fearless Amarr fleet was utterly surprised by an enemy that possessed incredible destructive power and remarkably advanced battle tactics. This, coupled with the unforgivable impetuousness of our fleet's leadership, resulted in the near-total annihilation of our warships, at an estimated cost of only one-third of the Jovian armada. We were never again to take to the field of battle against that most dangerous and mysterious opponent. However, while some ships escaped, in less than six hours of battle we left behind a vast field of our dead and dying ships. Today, this system – known now only as Atioth – holds almost none of these battlefield remains, having long since been swept clean by Amarr salvagers and various scavengers. Nonetheless, this system remains an eternal reminder of the vigilance and bravery of our Grand Fleet and the sacrifices they are often called on to make in service of the Empire.

Well, pilot, I could have at least understood refusing this mission in the first place. At least that would have been somewhat understandable given the value nature of the threat. But to quit in mid-shipment is something we did not expect from you. We shall retrieve the chips and deliver them ourselves.
Thank you, pilot. You will be doing the Empire a great service in even such a brief undertaking as this.

You have made a significant contribution to the Empire, pilot. We cannot thank you enough. Of course, no record will be kept of your part in this episode, as we cannot be seen to have been even slightly concerned over the risk of attack and the potential loss of these chips. We will, however, fulfill our financial obligation, as outlined in the mission contract.

I can understand your reluctance to undertake this mission, as we do not know who or what might be out there waiting to attack you in order to obtain these chips. This is a rare moment in that we bear you no malice for your fear.
Please remain off this comms channel, pilot. While your voice is encrypted, the communication itself can be hacked. Contact us only after docking, or, of course in the event you are attacked.
The Battle of Vak-Atioth

Some decades ago, Amarr veterinary scientists achieved a milestone in genetic manipulation with the creation of hybrid slaver hounds. These new breeds are specifically designed to live and work in extreme climate conditions, which is a boon for all those slave labor facilities on ice planets and other harsh environments. Demand for these animals has been overwhelming and we are struggling to maintain our delivery schedule. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station. From there they will be transshipped to a desert planet and put to work as guard animals.
I really am surprised that you're declining this one. It was a good chance to make some quick ISK with very little risk. Well, no bother. There is no shortage of pilots looking for an easy trip.

Amarr slavers on Syrikos V first learned to breed and train slaver hounds to provide an extra layer of low-cost security for their slave labor operations. These animals soon proved their worth, particularly as a last line of defense for any slave that managed to bypass a facility's security controls and escape into the whatever wilderness lay beyond the facility's walls. So keen are the senses of these animals, and so lethal their attacks, that most slaves will give up any hope of escape before even making the attempt. One problem that arose, however, was that many slave labor operations were located in some of the harshest imaginable environments, often so harsh that they were unsuitable for your average slaver hound.

So, it was with tremendous satisfaction that Amarr veterinary scientists reported recently that they had managed to create stable, obedient hybrids of the breed, each type adapted for a different geographic or atmospheric condition. Thus, if you are a slave owner on an ice planet, for example, you can now purchase slaver hounds with thicker pelts, greater body fat, and higher overall tolerance to cold and freezing wind. These new hybrids have proven remarkably adaptable, and have long since spread to slave labor facilities throughout the Empire.
Good to know the hounds haven't caused you any trouble. Please contact me when you reach the station. Offloading has already been arranged.
You're quitting this mission? You should know that quitting a mission as simple as this one does not look good on a pilot's record.
