The Origins of Hybrid Slaver Hounds

See? I told you this one was a no-brainer.  I would suggest, though, remaining in your ship until the hounds have been safely offloaded. I wouldn't want to be hanging around your cargo bay if one of them got loose, as the sedatives will have worn off by now.
I had a feeling an easy job like this one might interest you. Good chance to flip on the autopilot and take a nap.  Just make sure the cages are secure and locked and your cargo bay doors are sealed.

I'm not sure how much you know about Amarr slave labor installations, such as mines, agricultural harvesting fields, moon mineral extraction zones, and the like. Well, I can tell you that these facilities are often of such size and complexity that they cannot always be wholly secured against slave escape attempts. Certainly, all but the most primitive and poorly administrated of these locations feature any and all manner of perimeter alarms, security cameras, remote sentry drones, microwave motion detectors, infrared barrier fences, you name it. As you can imagine, though, this can get quite expensive given not only the capital outlay for the equipment, but for the manpower needed to operate and maintain them year-round, 24 hours a day.

It was during this search for lower cost alternatives to these technologies that the animals we call slaver hounds were introduced to the overall security plans of select slave labor facilities, used to detect, track, and interdict runaway slaves. Their acutely tuned senses coupled with their remarkable natural endurance and speed made them an ideal choice for many Amarr slave operations. However, it was not long before it was realized that the standard, purebred slaver hound was not suitable for all environments. This resulted in the creation of genetically modified breeds more at home in harsher environments such as swamps, frozen wastelands, jungles, and the like. Today, these more adaptable variants can be found on many such installations throughout the Empire, despite their comparatively high cost when compared to your usual slaver hounds.

This brings us to the reason I contacted you. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station for transshipment to an Amarr desert planet. As long as the hounds remain sedated and don't find their way out of their cages, this should be a simple, trouble-free courier job.

Yes, I think I have some work for you.

One of our research outposts in Molden Heath came under attack by rogue drones last week. This is highly unusual, since drones are rarely seen beyond Etherium Reach. The outpost's defense systems managed to keep our scientists safe, and the downed drones were retrieved for examination. They found unusual mineral deposits replacing the drones' original microboard networks, which appear to work far more efficiently.

Of course we don't want anyone else getting ahold of the samples before we can replicate them. The samples have been in transit via a series of drops in order to keep them safe. Take them on to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I can't wait to see what we've got.
Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.
Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.
{[character]player.name}, have you done what I asked?
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. We're one step closer to the forefront of technological advancement!

One of my clients asked me to send over drones to replace the ones his company's been losing in the line of work. That's all he said. He never said anything about needing mining drones; of course I sent him a set of scout drones, and he was very upset at me for not being able to read his mind. People should be more specific about things. Take these mining drones over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for him, and if he asks why the paint looks new, tell him they're fresh off the production line.
Just make sure to tell him how sorry I am, okay?
Fine. I can always find someone else.
I am very disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?
Excellent. I've been trying to get those old things off my hands for months.
I accidentally sent a client the wrong set of drones because they never specified what type he needed. Take the right cargo to him. Hopefully he won't ask too many questions.
Pilots' Little Helpers

After the successes of the first drones in the first Caldari-Gallente war, every empire set out to design a combat drone that suited their particular combat needs, though the small, pilotless tools clearly suited some empires' needs more than others. The Gallente company, CreoDron, has flourished, while the Carthum Conglomerate in Amarr maintains drone production more as a counter to their rival, Khanid Innovation, which stresses a reliance on rocket technology. Minmatar-based Boundless Creation has profited easily from drone production, but not enough to justify a specialized branch of operations; similarly, Ishukone in the Caldari State produces drones simply because demand exists rather than a desire to encourage a reliance upon them.

Like any other drone, a mining drone is simply an extension of a pilot's control. Unlike combat drones, mining drones have no offensive or defensive capabilities. Wastage factors for individual drones can be quite high, but the speed and convenience of having several extra mining lasers at the pilot's disposal outweighs the mineral loss.

While examining wrecked rogue drones following a failed attack, strange minerals were found which replaced some of the drones' usual systems. The compounds seem to run more efficiently than the parts they replaced, and your agent has hired you to take the find to researchers for examination.
Drones On Their Own

Once part of a Gallente scientist's experiments in self-controlled drone technology, rogue drones can now be found throughout the cluster, having escaped and begun to replicate themselves. In certain undeveloped parts of null-security space they thrive and expand their numbers from hives hidden deep within deadspace pockets and asteroid fields. These regions are called ‘drone regions', and the only people brave enough and confident enough to attempt to build out there are the capsuleers.

Our spies have succeeded in smuggling pieces of the latest experimental Amarrian starship technology back to the Republic. I need you to take the samples on to the lab where they can be properly analyzed.

You need to keep this quiet, {[character]player.name}. I know you capsuleers aren't accustomed to being told how to do your job, but this is bigger than anything else and if word gets out, all this effort will be for nothing.

We've acquired samples of the Amarr's latest experimental starship tech. Don't ask me how, I don't want to know, and neither do you. We're not sure what these pieces do; our source is suggesting it's a system that reduces the effectiveness of our electronic warfare systems. This could be bad news for us. Get the stuff over to the lab at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. And keep your trap shut. We don't want it getting back to the Amarr that we have this.
Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I knew we could count on you.
I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.
I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.
Have you delivered that stuff to the lab, {[character]player.name}?

Good job, {[character]player.name}. Our research team is saying the tech deflects target painter beams away towards an area of space just behind the ship it's fitted on. Our torpedoes will start missing targets if they manage to make this widely available. We need to find a way to counter this, and fast.
Weapon of Choice

The Minmatar Republic's reliance on speed for the majority of its fleet comes at a cost: up close, high transversal speed reduces the chance to hit the target, while fighting at distance brings fleet ships to the edge of their falloff range. The more mass a target has, the less difficult it is to react and hit. Target painters were eventually developed for the Republic's electronic warfare division, low-yield lasers which increase the mass profile of a target and reduce the negative effects of fighters moving at high velocity.
Planetary officials have asked me to bring in a team of mercenaries they've hired to deal with a terrorist threat. Your job is to keep them in line en route.

We have a planetary situation we need your help with. A group of pro-Amarr terrorists is wreaking havoc in outlying provinces, and the local government's hired a group of mercenaries to deal with them. You know mercs, I'm sure; they never really listen to anyone they think is softer than they are. We're having trouble finding an ordinary captain who's willing to ferry the guys over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for transit planetside. I think they'll be more likely to behave if the captain is someone who can and will follow through on a threat to vent the ship to vacuum. Someone like you, in other words. Can we count on you to keep the unruly lot in line?
Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! Don't actually vent the ship, though. We need these guys.
Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.
Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.
Those mercs aren't giving you too much trouble, I hope.
Excellent, {[character]player.name}! I'll let the local government know their solution is on its way.
It's Only Business

Mercenaries often get a bad reputation from the few who go nuts while on assignment, cause unacceptable collateral damage and demand higher pay for the effort involved in discretion. The majority are reasonable businessmen, primarily ex-military, who take their work seriously and simply demand respect for the risks they take.
Our salvagers have built up a load of industrial-quality scrap metal to be used in ship building. I need you to take it to the reclamation facility so we can recover the useable parts.

Okay, here's one for you. Don't look at me like that. Yes, it's a load of metal scraps we need taken to a reclamation facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Contrary to popular belief, our ships are not made solely of scrap-metal, utility adhesive and chewing gum, but we do recycle extensively.

The reason I'm asking you to do this rather than hiring a much cheaper regular captain is that these bits are industrial quality, or they will be once they've been processed. They're worth a lot of cred on the black market – peanuts to you capsuleers, but a year's wages to anyone else.
Thanks, {[character]player.name}. It's not a glamorous job but someone's gotta do it.
I am very disappointed, {[character]player.name}.
Sad, {[character]player.name}. I had hoped you were the reliable sort.
Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?
Good! You've been a big help, {[character]player.name}.
Reclamation and Improvisation

In the early days of space travel, after so long under the yoke of Amarr, the Minmatar were required to make do with what little they could find, with limited facilities and funding. The ability to create space-worthy ships from the most unlikely of materials became legendary. In the present-day Republic, scarcity is no longer a problem, but materials are still stretched as far as engineers can make them go for the sake of pride in their efficiency.

A Nefantar House is relocating to a planet within the Republic, and we've had a tip-off that they're working against us for someone in the Empire. We've planted surveillance nanobots in a shipment of materials for their planetside home; take it over to the depot. The logs will show nothing amiss.

I hope I can trust you to be discreet, {[character]player.name}.

As part of a goodwill gesture to the Nefantar tribe, the Republic has offered allotments of planetary territory within our space on which to build embassies or summer homes or whatever else they need land for. I don't care what it is, I don't trust ‘em, but the government is determined to make sure we all get along.

Yesterday I got an alert from one of my colleagues; it seems one Nefantar house is in collusion with elements from the Empire. Obviously we can't just point fingers without evidence, but I'm in a perfect position to obtain that. The contractor they hired to design and build a house on their new property is a friend of mine. He's given us one shipment of interior facing materials to seed with nanite spyware. Take the load to the depot at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I know I can trust you to keep quiet about the additions to the cargo.
Thanks, {[character]player.name}. If anyone asks where those came from, the manifest will show their usual station.
I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
I'm beginning to question your loyalty, {[character]player.name}.
Have you delivered your cargo for me, {[character]player.name}?

Thanks to your assistance, {[character]player.name}, we've been able to record some rather incriminating communications from these people already. They wasted no time in contacting their associates in the Empire to let them know they were settled in.
Strained Relations

The day Drupar Maak struck down Arkon Ardishapur on Starkman Prime with the Heir's own sceptre began the darkest night for his people. In retribution for the death of his father and their attempted rebellion, Idonis Ardishapur ordered the annihilation of the Starkmanir tribe.

At the same time, the Nefantar tribe approached the Empire with an offer, making a bargain for mercy in exchange for assisting in the subjugation of the Minmatar. The tribe took on many aspects of the Empire, including open practise of their faith and owning Minmatar slaves, themselves. Despite the recent revelation that their conversion helped to protect the last Starkmanir to survive the purge, many within the Republic are hesitant to forgive the Nefantar for their actions.
One of our planetside subsidiaries has recently lost a lot of farming equipment to a storm. I need you to take these parts to the assembly plant so we can recoup our losses.

One of our subsidiaries has recently suffered a major setback, {[character]player.name}. A hurricane wiped out half their planetside crops and wrecked the equipment. Most of it was already falling apart, the storm just finished it off. Obviously, this is a big problem for them, and us, but it's still the early part of the first growing season. Deliver these parts to the assembly plant at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can replace the equipment before they lose too much from this harvest.
Thank you, {[character]player.name}.
I am greatly disappointed, {[character]player.name}.
I am greatly disappointed, {[character]player.name}.
Have you delivered those parts yet, {[character]player.name}?
Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. Our subsidiary has managed to save more than they first thought of the initial crops and they're good to go for the second growing season.
Acts of God

Recent decades have seen a resurgence in attempts to control planetary weather patterns on a full global scale, particularly on technologically advanced agricultural worlds. Ensuring a regular cycle of rain and sun enables farmers to plant crops throughout the year with a smaller margin for error.

Despite the advances, the most that can be claimed is weather ‘guidance'. The one successfully controlled year on Aforat in the Mishi system was followed by two years of raging, uncontrollable storms which flattened fields with hail and flooded river valleys. The blame was laid on aggressive methods exercised by the corporation in charge of the project; reactors placed within existing ocean currents prevented seawater from cooling regularly in the colder months, disrupting the planetary climate entirely.

Against my better judgment, I've been asked to order several sets of educational packages of the Amarr Scriptures for the children of families who have been released by the Empire. It leaves a sour taste in the mouth, but maybe we can use the teaching materials to our own ends.

I'm in a bit of an awkward position here, {[character]player.name}. With all the people being released from slavery in the Empire, we're getting more and more families who practice the Amarr religion. No thanks to Jamyl, she knew this would happen. The edict from our government is that we need to respect the poor deluded people and gently introduce them to a new way of thinking. It won't be easy, and it's putting a strain on all of us.

My problem right now is that a bunch of the refugee families have requested that some Amarr Scriptures be included in the course structure at the schools we've set up for their children. It's our own people doing the teaching, so we can slowly steer the education in the right direction, but we all still feel dirty for having to use it.

Do you think you'd be willing to take a shipment of books over to one of the schools?
Thanks, {[character]player.name}. I knew I could count on you.
I'm very disappointed, {[character]player.name}.
I'm very disappointed, {[character]player.name}.
Have you delivered those books, {[character]player.name}?
Thank you, {[character]player.name}. I know it's an unsavory business, but our instructions from on high are to try to get along and help these people adjust.
Necessary Concessions

With the release of several generations of slaves from the Empire, Jamyl struck a blow at the heart of Minmatar culture, forcing the Republic to accept those who have known only the ways of Amarr and what little Minmatar tradition they had been able to maintain through the years. Inducting such people into modern Republic society has proven troublesome and at times outright frustrating; allowing released slaves to practice the religion they grew up with has been a bitter necessity as counselors struggle to help the people adapt to their new lives.
Thank you, {[character]player.name}.
I am most disappointed.
Disappointing, {[character]player.name}.
I haven't received confirmation of your delivery yet, {[character]player.name}. Is there a problem?

Thank you, {[character]player.name}. The testers have already submitted a preliminary report; looks like the formula needs some work. They say it's not enough of an improvement on the current industry standard to be worth producing on a large scale. One member of the team has suggested an application involving crystalline fullerides and dropping C86 entirely; it'll have to go up for review.
Speed-Tanking

Smaller ships rely upon their speed and smaller signature radius to make it difficult for larger ships to track and target them. The heat output from propulsion systems increases signature radius, making a small target much easier to track; the greater the speed, the greater the heat production. Specialized coatings help to reduce the effect and prevent expansion of the parts within propulsion systems, helping them to operate much more efficiently.
I have to request a difficult task of you: play nice with a swarm of Angel Cartel representatives and their entourage on your ship. Hopefully they won't try to cause you trouble.

This is a list of people I want you to escort to a meeting. They have quite a large security entourage, and as you can see from some of the names, they have a reason for it. These people are members of the Angel Cartel. While the Cartel are thugs and pirate scum, and are not particularly welcome in Minmatar space, it does not mean that some corporations don't have certain dealings with them which require us to overlook certain... failings.

Escort them safely to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. It's nothing you'll be in trouble with the Republic for, but for the sake of our business relations, try to treat them politely.
Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Please hurry.
I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}, but I can understand why you might decline.
I'm extremely disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
Hello, {[character]player.name}. Have you finished your work for me?
Excellent, thank you, {[character]player.name}.
Borderland Outlaws

The Angel Cartel's reputation for engaging in any activity regardless of its legality has earned it the DED's description of the most dangerous criminal organization in the cluster. With a corporate command structure and open recruitment policy, the Cartel are less thugs than sharks in pinstripe suits, capable of operating on all levels of society. With a major operational base in Etherium Reach on the edge of Minmatar space, the Cartel is held with deep suspicion within the Republic. Their annexation of the Skarkon system in YC 110 and sudden withdrawal left many unanswered questions regarding both the Cartel's intentions towards the Republic and what deals were forged under the table to make them leave... and what those deals might have cost.

A pair of civilians too wealthy for their own good are holding a decadent reception for their wedding, and ordered a tremendously expensive champagne to keep their guests entertained. A regular pilot can't be trusted to ship the drinks in, but what's a thousand-ISK bottle of wine to a capsuleer?

You must have heard of Chaylie Vann. No? What rock have you been living under? She's a big-name actress, does a lot of calculated lobbying for various charities in Placid, and she's getting married to some seriously old-money geezer from Intaki – yeah, we all know how that relationship is going to end. Never mind that. They're paying big bucks for an extravagant reception at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and put in a massive order for Feille d'Marnne in order to keep their guests happy.

Feille d'Marnne is some seriously posh champagne, {[character]player.name}. Each case of this stuff costs as much as an Incursus, and they're buying more than one. Obviously, we can't trust anyone less than a capsuleer to deliver the lot – an ordinary pilot would be more likely to run the stuff onto the black market.
Thanks, {[character]player.name}, I knew we could count on you.
Fine, I'll find someone else, hopefully before it's too late.
I'm not laughing, {[character]player.name}. I have a reputation to maintain, you know.
I haven't received a receipt for that champagne yet. What's the hold up?

Thank you, {[character]player.name}. I was able to secure an invitation to the reception thanks to your work. You should have seen the old man staggering around after hoarding several bottles of the champagne. He and Vann got into an argument towards the end of the night; turns out neither of them was as well-off as they appeared to be, even to each other, and they couldn't afford to pay the event bill. It's the latest scandal, the news services are all over it.
The Entertainment Game

Nobody loves a good party more than the Gallente. The hedonistic stereotype is one that the Federation revels in and flaunts shamelessly. Public figures actively compete to host the wildest and most fashionable affairs, vying for the attention of news services and gossip magazines. Among the celebrity elite, a wedding, birth or even a funeral is simply another excuse to splash out and stand in the limelight.

A friend and I are running a small holoreel bootlegging operation on the side. The shipments are bound for Syndicate, but I only need you to take them on to where my business partner is operating from.

I like nice things, {[character]player.name}. Who doesn't? Handing missions out to you people all day doesn't offer nearly enough to cover my expenses, so a friend and I run a shipping business out to Syndicate space. Nothing big enough to interfere with the Syndicate itself, mind you. We provide a humanitarian service importing the latest holos from the heart of civilization. It's the only way they can get the things for a reasonable cost – buying them direct from the companies in the Federation incurs immense shipping charges.

Our usual courier is out of commission today, with her ship in for repairs after a pirate attack. If you want to make yourself useful, take the latest shipment over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and ask for Amelyn. They'll know who you mean, just say that “Imba” sent you.
Good, good.
Fine. It's not like anyone would believe you if you told them, anyway.
Fine. It's not like anyone would believe you if you told them, anyway.
Amelyn hasn't contacted me yet, {[character]player.name}. What's the hold up?

Thanks for your help, {[character]player.name}. Turns out our normal courier sold us out; the hangar we normally use was raided just after you left for your cargo run and officials from the Federal Performance Rights Union came around asking nosy questions. Good thing we were using your hangar, huh?
The Syndicate Market

The Syndicate is the underbelly of Federation society, filled with its outcasts and criminals; it's a place where they can move freely and openly, and even prosper outside the reach of the law. As a result, supplies of luxury items at affordable rates are hard to come by, leading to a thriving black market in everything from sweets and the latest fashions from the Crystal Boulevard to ship parts and broadcasting equipment.

For those who reside under the independent governorship of the station managers, life can be more expensive when acquired legally. Official companies within the Federation add a high tariff for the risk of shipping through low-security and lawless space; the more frequent the attacks, the higher the cost. Residents who aspire to a higher-quality life must live with a daily balancing act of legality and affordability. Even such minor offenses as purchasing necessities via the black markets can potentially bar an otherwise law-abiding citizen from finding an honest living within Empire space.
I accidentally sent the wrong shipment over to another laboratory. I need to you take these frogs over; it's the right shipment, this time, I'm positive!

Yes, yes, perhaps you could help me out.

A few days ago, I was at one of those parties - you know the type, where they shoot you full of stims if you start to drag, and you just keep going until reality starts to fold in on itself and turn into confetti, and there's the scent of rosewater and….

To make a long story short, I accidentally sent the wrong cargo over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. They were less than amused to receive a crate of live Intaki peepers rather than the cryo-stored Luminaire skippers they needed. One frog is much like another, but the pet-shop variety make very poor laboratory testing groups. Take these over, and they may forgive me enough to require my services in the future.
Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I doubt they'll give the peepers back, since they all escaped into the labs when the box was opened, but it's worth asking.
You needn't get snooty about it. As if you've never made errors under the influence before.
But what about my frogs?
Have you delivered those frogs yet, {[character]player.name}?
You're a career-saver, {[character]player.name}.
Animal Testing

In laboratory work, animals are still used occasionally for testing in appropriate situations. The most popular subjects are Luminaire skippers, a common amphibian from Gallente Prime, and Harst's Greater Earless Rat, which is actually a kind of marsupial of indeterminate origin due to its habit of hitching rides in ship cargo holds.

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has a number of outposts in w-space systems, exploring what lies beyond known space. They've turned up some unusual pieces which I need you to take to a more extensive laboratory for identification.

Yes, I have some work for you.

We have several research outposts in various w-space systems. It's one of those things that nobody discusses but everybody knows about anyway. They've recovered bits of ancient technology which seem to have unusual properties... well, compared to what we're used to seeing, at least. We're hoping these might be a clue to the Sleepers' technology... but it could easily be remnants of a scrapyard, for all we know. Take these samples over to the lab at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, so we can figure out what we've got.
Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Hurry up! This could be our biggest breakthrough yet!
If it's not worth your time, you could have just said so.
This displeases me, {[character]player.name}.
I've not received a receipt for the cargo yet, {[character]player.name}.
Excellent!
Corporate W-Space Exploration

Capsuleers aren't the only people to explore the systems accessible via wormholes. Every corporation wants to be the first to make the Next Big Discovery, and then market the developments from researching it. Most corporations will categorically deny that this is what they're doing, creating an atmosphere of both paranoia and plausible deniability if their explorations turn up nothing of value.

A nearby station has suffered a life-support failure. They got the atmospheric regulators working again, but the interior temperature is starting to drop. Get the heating units over there quickly, before the place gets too cold.

A severe accident has occurred on another station, {[character]player.name}; they suffered a freak blowout in primary life-support and the station's environmental control shut down entirely. No, don't panic, they stabilized the atmosphere as soon as they could, so the people on the station won't asphyxiate. But the internal heating units have yet to be replaced. People are bundling up as their heat bleeds out – the external insulation is some protection, but it's not enough.

To help out, we've put together as many portable emergency heating units as we could find on such short notice. Take them over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and quickly!
Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}.
Well, I'm certain we can find someone who values their job more.
You're heartless, {[character]player.name}. What about all those people?
Have you delivered the heating units yet?
Great to hear, {[character]player.name}!
Station-Side Survival

The most vital systems on a space station or starship, life-support covers everything from atmosphere generation and recycling to environmental control to the recycling of drinking and pumping water. Originally a series of tanks containing specialized filters, as residence in space extended from long-term to lifetimes, advances in bioengineering developed hydroponics systems for stations which both produce and recycle air and water efficiently. Environmental control, which cycles water and air through the station and maintains an even internal temperature despite the cold of space outside nibbling at the edges, runs off the same generator as the internal electrical circuits. External electrical devices, such as guide-lights, shielding and containment fields, security systems and communications, run from separate generators with extensive backup arrays.
One of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s archaeological teams has uncovered a load of pre-Federation relics. I need you to transport the pieces to a laboratory for analysis.

One of our archaeological teams has unearthed a load of pre-Federation tech from a moon in this system. We're really excited about this; I don't think I need to explain to you how the results of this find could give us a leg up on the competition. Get this lot over to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and don't tell anyone!
Good to hear!
Sad. I thought you'd have more interest than that.
This greatly displeases me, {[character]player.name}.
{[character]player.name}, have you delivered those artifacts yet?
Excellent! We'll get started on the analysis immediately. This is so exciting!
Retro Revival

Corporations often sponsor archaeological and research projects, paying for work permits and equipment when the people involved need them. In exchange, the corporations obtain exclusive rights to any discoveries which are made. This includes the right to display and charge viewing fees, or to make new developments based upon information obtained from the artifacts.

This shipment of Cerrocentite needs to be taken to the manufacturer on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The cargo is radioactive, and while the containment units are good enough for a short period, the mineral really requires an industrial containment in a stable and controlled environment.

Okay, take a look at this. You know what this is? Yes, yes, it's a rock. It's a rare mineral, actually, called Cerrocentite. It has industrial applications, but it's mostly used in security systems. The reason it's in a special containment field is that it's also fairly radioactive. Take this shipment over to the manufacturers at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't bloody open it!
Thanks, {[character]player.name}. Do try to hurry, you don't want this stuff sitting around too long in your cargo hold.
I am disappointed, {[character]player.name}.
I am disappointed, {[character]player.name}.
Have you delivered that Cerrocentite, {[character]player.name}? You don't want to expose your ship to it for much longer.
Good to hear, {[character]player.name}!
Redundant Systems

Security systems on stations are all-in-one, monitoring room occupancy, ambient temperature and humidity, and the gas mix from environmental control. It can be set to go on alert for various stimuli, and contains several redundant systems to ensure that an interrupt on one line does not prevent a problem being reported. Small pieces of radioactive material which are sensitive to various stimuli are an integral part of such systems.

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is hosting a fashion show for publicity, and your agent needs you to pick up the models. For some reason, they think you won't get fed up and drop them all off in orbit around the nearest moon.

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is playing host to a fashion show. It's just another publicity stunt, but we need something to gain the public eye again.

We need someone to pick up the models and fashionistas from {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. You can kind of guess what they're like – a normal pilot just isn't good enough for them, so I have to find a capsuleer I think is level-headed enough to not vent cargo into space if they get too annoying. I know you can handle it, it's not like you have to speak with them face to face, anyway.
Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I'll make it worth your while.
Regrettable, but I can't say I blame you, {[character]player.name}.
I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. We have a reputation to maintain.
Have you picked up the models yet? The show's only a few hours away!
Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! Tonight's show should be spectacular.
The Business of Art

Like most small corporate entities relying on creativity and artistry, Gallente fashion houses frequently accept patronage from larger corporations, which then sponsor shows and displays. The artists benefit from the visibility and the patron corporations gain another reason to be in the news. Occasionally, the artists incorporate symbols relating to their sponsors in their work, such as logos, corporate colors and mantras, or materials produced by the company.

As always, some art houses denounce the practice, stating that corporate ties bias the work produced by the artists, and accuse the other artists of “selling out,” sacrificing their autonomy for a little planetary cred.

The Natural Way is a group which promotes a lower-tech way of life. They're throwing around a lot of cred to start a fitness initiative encouraging kids to stay away from body modding, and I see nothing wrong with encouraging them in exchange for a little ISK.
Just don't watch those, okay? They gave me nightmares.
What? Who doesn't want to take advantage of anti-tech crazies?
Well, fine. But burn the holos. We don't want normal people watching that stuff.
You haven't WATCHED those, have you?
Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. My mother's been giving those to my kids for their birthdays every year, and I was afraid I'd never get rid of them.
The Natural Way

There was a time when our children roamed free beneath the sun. They grew strong and healthy under the clear breezes and warm rains. But then technology arose, and with it pollution, sedentary lifestyles, and then the means to compensate for it artificially. But is this truly healthy? Instead of living naturally long lifespans, we turn to medicine and modifications to improve ourselves. Today's teenager spends their days in front of a holoscreen; many of them don't even leave the house of their parents to attend school, preferring to interface remotely.

My friends, is this how we want our children to live?” -- Excerpt from The Natural Way's introductory leaflet

I'm sure you're all too aware of our war with the Caldari State. It's been dragging on for years with no end in sight... until now, that is. We've been making some good headway on the active front and our research and development has been busy behind the scenes. Military scientists have developed a hybrid round that works like single-target burst ECM, and it's time to introduce it to the military for an active field-test.

Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
Do not fail us, {[character]player.name}. The Federation is depending on you.
I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought your loyalty might mean more to you.
I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. If we find that you've shared this with the Caldari, it will not go well for you.
Have you finished your delivery, {[character]player.name}?
Thank you, {[character]player.name}. You are a true child of the Federation.
Brothers in Arms Race

Despite their origins in the same solar system, the history between the Gallente Federation and the Caldari State has been laced with conflict since the early days. Initially unified in reaching to the stars through the development of stargate technology, relations rapidly degenerated after the Caldari struck out on their own. Now, separated by a closely-watched border zone, the focus of the two empires lies in staying a few steps ahead of each other.

A small fleet of unidentified frigates has attacked one of our remote communications outposts, killing and injuring dozens of our personnel. Those who survived the attack managed to pilot a high-speed shuttle to the nearest station. However, we have strong reason to believe that a team of assassins is en route to their location to eliminate them before they can pass along the information about the organization responsible for this attack. We need you to make all possible haste to their location and rescue the survivors before this hit team arrives.

We are disappointed that you have chosen not to complete this critical mission; you've left our contractors at great risk. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere, though I doubt this will be possible at this late stage.
Your refusal to accept this mission will undoubtedly result in numerous civilian casualties. We must now try to find someone else to undertake this rescue operation.

Your skillful handing of your ship in this vital rescue mission has saved the lives of many civilians who would have otherwise surely perished in the damaged outpost. We knew we could count on you and we will now move you to the top of our list for future missions.

Earlier today, a small, unknown group of frigates attacked one of our remote signals intelligence (SIGINT) communications outposts, causing catastrophic damage and killing dozens of our personnel. This station belongs – or should I say belonged - to a small Caldari corporation with a poorly hidden contractual link to our military intelligence services. Fortunately, the survivors managed to escape, via their high-speed emergency shuttle and are expected to arrive at a nearby station within the hour.

As you might expect, we are working hard to determine the identities of the aggressors, but as yet we have no solid leads. Of course, this is not your concern. What is your concern, should you choose to help us, is a report we just received indicating that the surviving team of SIGINT contractors have been targeted for immediate assassination by the same mysterious organization behind the outpost attack. Apparently, someone does not want these individuals to provide us with whatever information they must have obtained during the course of their recent duties.

Within the last few hours, we intercepted a poorly encrypted communication indicating that a covert hit squad is en route to the station aboard an unspecified vessel – or may actually be at the station already! This station's security force, while well armed and highly trained, is insufficient to detect and defeat the kind of lethal operatives that we believe intend to kill our contractors. Therefore, we need you to rescue this team immediately and bring them back to us for an emergency debriefing and to ensure their safety.

After running a check of qualified pilots in our office database, your name was near the top of the list. We estimate there will only be sufficient time for this one rescue attempt before the assassins strike.
Caldari SIGINT Outpost Network

The Caldari Navy, much like the military services of other races, operates a covert network of signals intelligence outposts along the borders of the Caldari State. The specific, primary mission of these stations is to provide advance early warning of any hostile incursion by the Gallente military. Beyond this vital mission, however, the outposts are also tasked with gathering intelligence on a wide variety of other targets, both military and civilian. Of particular interest is the regular provision of information on the movement of the commercial and industrial fleets of other races, given the competition between the Caldari corporate system and foreign companies. In this way, the outposts not only provide an essential early warning system for any hostile forces, but also provide data of immense economic value, thus better enabling the Caldari private business sector to better compete in the merciless realm of interstellar business.

There is no time to discuss this mission further given the haste with which you will need to accomplish this. Please contact me only when you have delivered the contractors safely to the final destination.
Thank you for agreeing to attempt the rescue of our civilian contractors. You must leave very soon if we are to have any hope of reaching them before the hit team arrives.

Amarr scientists, working at a clandestine engineering laboratory in a nearby system may have developed the hardest metal yet known to science, known as Ditanium. The potential applications for warfare, specifically, in hardening our warships, is simply too tempting to pass up. Therefore, the full weight of the Amarr military science machine is waiting eagerly for the results of the pending tests, in which the Ditanium plates will be affixed to a specially modified frigate for flight testing. Therefore, we need you to deliver a large quantity of these plates to a nearby station where it will be transshipped to a military shipyard for fitting to the Punisher testbed ship.

As you know, Amarr warships rely heavily on the various armors that we use in the construction and upgrading of our ships. For the most part, we rely on the same metals and alloys found in markets and hangars found in virtually every corner of the populated regions. Thus, it is a rare thing when a wholly new metal appears – and rarer still when only one race discovers it, unbeknownst to the others.

Such an occurrence, I can tell you now only in the strictest confidence, has indeed taken place at a remote clandestine Amarr metallurgical research facility. Masquerading as a routine ore processing laboratory near an otherwise uninteresting Veldspar-laden asteroid field, this facility has been conducting advanced research exclusively into an extremely rare and highly classified metal, found only in the ore of a small fraction of the asteroids present in that specific field: a new metal we call Ditanium. To date, this is the strongest naturally occurring metal yet encountered by our scientists. While we are confident that this metal exists elsewhere in space, to our knowledge, we are the first to actually find it.

Given the rarity of this metal and the significant complexities of its mining and processing, it has taken two full months to produce just enough finished metal plates to fit a single Punisher-class frigate. We intend to use this ship for Phase I field testing, which includes flight handling characteristics, radar cross-section analysis, temperature extremes testing, and other critical operational parameters. If successful, we are confident that we may be able to begin full scale production and ship fitting within two years.

However, before this test can take place, we need someone to courier these Ditanium plates to a station we designate. From there, it will be transshipped to a military shipyard for fitting to the Punisher testbed ship. We do not anticipate this shipment will present any problems, particularly given the high level of secrecy relating to the project, but with potentially many hundreds of billions of ISK riding on the successful integration of Ditanium into our armor plates and other protective ship components, we are taking no chances.

We need to know immediately if you will deliver this Ditanium to the designated station.

I was just informed that you have chosen to quit this important mission prior to the agreed on completion conditions. Please return the Ditanium plates to the nearest Amarr station and we will consider this arrangement terminated.

Well, it is unfortunate that you've chosen not to help us. We trust that you will not discuss this meeting with any other parties, though we are confident that if you did, they would likely laugh you out of whatever station bar you frequent. And if we do hear of you babbling your mouth about this, be assured that we will find you and liquidate any chance of a future partnership, if you catch my meaning.

Outstanding news, {[character]player.name}. Our scientists have verified receipt of the Ditanium plates and are right now moving those pallets to other ships for transshipment to the final destination. Well done and please contact us again in the future should you seek further employment. And remember: you were never here.
Yes, well, we were quite confident that this would be a fairly routine mission, so we were glad to hear that is indeed the case. Fly safe, pilot.

We have reason to believe that a small team of Gallente saboteurs has managed to destroy one of our new – and not yet fully operational – Command Centers on a nearby ice planet. These facilities are critical elements in our overall plan to dominate the planet such that we can then exploit the vast and lucrative materials that we have identified there in abundance. We need you to deliver a large complement of Arctic Warfare Marines to a forward station so that they can then be transferred down to provide the security we so desperately need. Their massive amounts of equipment will be brought in on other ships, so we need you to deliver these men safely and securely – everything depends on their safe arrival.
Need to Know
Are the Marines behaving themselves? Good. Please continue to make all possible haste in delivering them to the station. They tend to get a bit rowdy when they are cooped up too long.

How you can quit this mission mid-stream is absolutely beyond me. Do you have any idea the mountains of isk that this is going to cause my department and the Planetary Exploitation Division as a whole? Don't ever come back here for a while.

I'm glad to you hear that you've agreed to help us out on this one. If you'll just confirm this manifest, we'll rally the Marines and have them report to your ship immediately. You'd better get moving – don't want to keep the troops waiting.

We have so far managed to keep this event a closely held secret, as we do not want to discourage the senior management of the company from further exploiting the extremely valuable materials that are in largely untapped abundance on the sea floor. If word of this was to get out at this critical stage, it might give them reason pack up and move to a safer location - perhaps even to another planet. Well, this would simply be unacceptable, as our new planetary industry efforts have so far generated record revenues - the one thing keeping our shareholders and investors happy. And we want to keep them happy, if you understand my meaning. We must allow nothing to interrupt that flow of ISK into our corporate coffers.

I just got word that you delivered all the Marines safely to the station, great job! However, I must now coordinate the follow-on shipment of their equipment and weapons, which is going to mean another all-nighter here at the office. Oh well, business first, yes?  We will be in touch for future missions, so thanks again.

That you have chosen to decline this mission has put this company in a very difficult position, to say the least. Well, get out of here then; let us hope the Marines don't hear about this and decide to give you a rather rough send-off.

Two days ago, a covert Gallente strike team infiltrated and destroyed a brand new Command Center on a nearby ice planet. We think they managed to infiltrate as local civilian workers due the fact that the facility's Personnel Security Identification Systems had not yet been fully brought online. This unforgivable lapse in security enabled the four-man team to gain access to a highly secure area that contains the controls for the counter-harmonic stabilizers which, in short, keep the entire facility level and secure in the very harsh climates encountered on that planet. A series of well-placed explosives damaged these stabilizers, however, taking them offline and causing the entire command center to collapse and sink through the ice to the ocean floor some two kilometers below. Fortunately, the bulk of the work force was not scheduled to arrive for two more weeks, so casualties were very light. The financial and economic costs were, however, staggering.

Now that you understand the gravity of the situation, we can proceed to the reason that we contacted you to help us in this critical moment in the company's ongoing rapid expansion phase. We need you to very quietly transport a company of our best Arctic Warfare Marines from this station to the destination station with all possible haste. From there they will flown to the ice planet to provide a very high level of security for this and other nearby command centers and facilities. It is just a matter of time before this disastrous event becomes public knowledge, and we need to prove to the senior management, shareholders, and investors that we have the security situation resolutely in hand.

So, {[character]player.name}, are you willing to help us out by delivering a large number of Arctic Marines to the designated station?

The daughter of a Caldari executive was kidnapped this morning by a group of slavers while she was on holiday. They are demanding we provide them a large quantity of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium, in exchange for her life. There is no time to mount a rescue operation, so our only choice is to provide this shipment immediately. We will deal with those criminals once the girl has been released to us. However, time is of the essence, and our primary mission now is to deliver this shipment to a transshipment station for further transportation to the slavers' designated rendezvous point.

Time is a factor here, so I will get to the point. The daughter of a prominent Caldari industrialist, CEO of a large scrap metal corporation, was kidnapped while she was on holiday with her school classmates. At the time of her abduction, she was in a lowsec system she should not have been in, one well known for its hedonistic night life. Apparently, the girls each told a bit of a fib to their parents, indicating they were traveling to a much safer, highsec destination resort. Well, early this morning we received an urgent call from the executive's chief of security telling us that the daughter had been grabbed and thrown into a vehicle by some dangerous-looking men outside a bar after a night of drinking.

While we had hoped it was part of some prank or a misunderstanding as to what the girls really saw, our worst fears have been realized. We have been contacted, through a circuitous channel, by a notorious band of slavers. As proof of life, they have transmitted the daughter's DNA sequence to us. Analysis of this information has verified her identity.

The kidnappers have given us a very short window in which we can secure the girl's safe release, after which they will sell her into slavery – and I don't want to even imagine what horrors that might entail. As expected, they are demanding a very large payoff in exchange for her life. Specifically, they want our entire stockpile of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium – one found only in the wiring of electronic countermeasures (ECM) equipment of the Caldari Navy's Rook-class combat reconnaissance ships.

What I need you to do is to quickly move this quantrium to the designated station for transshipment to the slavers' rendezvous point. We will take it from there.

Please, pilot, do make haste. The quantrium must be delivered as soon as possible. If we are even one minute late to the rendezvous, the slavers will assume we have involved the authorities, and we will never see the young girl again.

The kidnappers have been listening to our comms, and have heard that you have chosen to quit. They have let us know that we will not see the executive's daughter again. I hope your reasons for quitting are worth the life of an innocent young girl.
We were counting on you. You were our only hope for the safe return of the CEO's daughter. I hope your cowardice here today will haunt you for the rest of your miserable life!

We just got word from the hotel security staff – the executive's daughter was returned to them safe and sound, as the kidnappers promised!  We owe you a debt I hope we can repay one day! We will not forget you!

Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. During a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's sensor cross-section, making it much easier to detect and attack. Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Therefore, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet.

Greetings, {[character]player.name}. Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. He swallowed a hidden poison tablet as we moved in to arrest him, so he is no longer a threat.

However, during a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's signature radius, making it much easier for our enemies to detect and attack.

Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Essentially, the Widow's commander would not know that his ship had lost its critical operational advantage until he was detected and targeted by hostile combatants. Given the very specialized role of this ship, not only would the Widow be compromised, but it is possible than any ships he might be bridging in via its covert jump portal generator could be unknowingly hot dropped near a waiting enemy fleet, instead of empty space.

In order to remedy this critical situation, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet. This shipment represents our best and only hope to quickly repair the damage done by the Gallente spy and ensure the safety of our brave Widow pilots and crew.
Do not contact me on an open channel until this mission is complete. Remember, this is a clandestine operation!
Your successful delivery of the prototype nanites will undoubtedly save the lives of many Black Ops pilots and crew. You have the makings of a good counter operative!
We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our Black Ops teams at great risk. We will have to find another operative elsewhere.
We are disappointed that you've chosen not to accept this critical mission. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere.

Produced by the Kaalakiota megacorporation, the Widow-class Black Ops battleship represents the current edge technology for Caldari military vessels used in covert operations. The primary function of the Widow is to conduct infiltration and espionage behind enemy lines. Specifically, when equipped with covert cynosural field generators and covert jump portal generators, the ship can create a “bridge” through which conventional ships are instantly transported, much like a jump gate. The effect of this is to surprise an enemy by instantly “hot dropping” a combat fleet into what was, moments prior, only empty space. In addition, it can also be fitted with ECM modules and cruise missiles such that it can provide jamming capabilities and supporting firepower if necessary. Using this technology, the Widow represents a significant force multiplier in the ongoing conflicts faced by the Caldari State.
We are relieved to hear that you've accepted this important mission. It is imperative that you deliver this cargo with all possible haste.
Widow-class Black Ops Battleships

A team of mercenaries led by a man calling himself “Black Dog” has killed one of our senior managers as he toured an asteroid field not far from here. Intelligence has indicated that he intends to continue these operations into the foreseeable future. To remedy this unacceptable situation, we need you to transport a trained assassin and his entourage to a station closer to the scene of the crime. Once this is done, you will have completed the terms of this contract. We appreciate your discretion in this endeavor.
Corporate Assassins
We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our executives and even our miners at significant risk from these mercenaries.

Your unwillingness to assist us in this matter is going to cost this corporation a great deal of isk until we can find some other way to resolve it. Mr. Smith may soon take a personal interest in you, as you've now disrupted his lucrative contract. I certainly don't want to be in your shoes once he gets the word.

We all know the saying, “business is war.” Nowhere is this adage practiced more seriously than in the Caldari corporate world. The soldiers in this fight are typically thought of as the salesmen, managers, executives, and other boardroom warriors. However, from time to time a very special skill set is required to deal with an equally specific threat. For these situations, corporate assassins are sometimes required to resolve issues that cannot be otherwise remedied through conventional channels. In the most extreme cases, these highly-trained operatives, most of whom served particularly arduous and dangerous careers in the Caldari Special Forces and intelligence groups, are hired to carry out very selective missions with very limited goals. The missions they are paid, - highly paid at that - to undertake would rival any holovid espionage movie, though the consequences are, of course, much more serious. You don't want to mess with these guys, and gals, as it is usually the last thing you'll ever do.

We just received word from Mr. Smith that you did indeed deliver him on time and without attracting any unusual inquiries. We hope the compensation for this mission was worth your time. The Caldari State can use more competent and discretionary pilots like you.
Why are you contacting me?

Before we begin, I must make one thing perfectly clear: You were never here, and this meeting never took place. You do understand what I mean, yes?

We are in need of a pilot who can deliver a very sensitive cargo from this station to a nearby station, without attracting any undue attention. You may have heard in the news or the local gossip channels that a Caldari regional director for mining operations was murdered yesterday by unknown assailants while touring an asteroid field in his personal shuttle. That much is indeed true. However, what has not been reported is that we have, in the last few hours, learned the identity of the assassin, a mercenary who goes by the name “Black Dog”, and that he and his team have already begun to plan for an ongoing hit-and-run campaign designed to try and scare off Caldari corporations from any future mining activities in the region.

Of course, we cannot allow this kind of disruption to what has proven a highly lucrative endeavor – the Board and our shareholders simply will not tolerate any further dips in revenues. To remedy this interruption, one of our sister companies that specializes in, shall we say, discrete solutions, has loaned us one of their most highly trained specialists to resolve this issue. His name, as you might expect, is Mr. Smith. His mission, in brief, is to liquidate Black Dog, along with any associates that may be operating with him at the time.

What we need from you, and need soon, is for you to transport Mr. Smith and his entourage to a station closer to the action – one with a hangar walkway the leads directly to an unmarked office. Once you have dropped him off, your role in this action will be complete.

So, what is it going to be, pilot? We need a yes or no right now if this operation is to stay on schedule.
We know the mission is proceeding well, as we've got a cloaked Covert Ops ship following you at a discrete distance. Please contact me only in the event of an emergency.
I'm glad to hear you're going to help us out here. We aren't expecting any trouble with this one, but with corporate espionage, you never know – keep your eyes open.

By quitting mid-mission you've singlehandedly compromised the whole operation! I doubt we'll be able to flush out the spy now, given the fact that you've interrupted the shipment – no doubt he will sense something is up and simply remain unknown to us.
Well, we are disappointed that you've turned this one down. We'll have to use one of our own transportation pilots to get this done.

Outstanding job, {[character]player.name}! As you may have heard by now, the spy was caught trying to remove the device from the offload cargo bay on the station. Needless to say, he has a very uncomfortable future ahead of him in one of our interrogation facilities. Thanks to your piloting skills and discretion, our work on the new cloak remains a well guarded secret.

In order to get around the laws pertaining to the transportation of illegal drugs through Amarr Empire space, we have been forced to create new and unknown substances for use on, or by, rather, our various slave labor enclaves. This new drug, Blue Paradise, does away with many of the harmful chemicals previously used while actually increasing the pleasurable effects. We are certain that, properly controlled and distributed, introduction of this drug into the slave labor workforce will increase productivity by a substantial margin. We are counting on you to deliver it to the designation transshipment station as soon as possible.
Biochemical Agents for Improved Slave Workloads
Well, you have certainly wasted my very valuable time. I thought we could count on you, but obviously I was misinformed. Don't count on working for me any time soon.

Excellent. We are transferring your cargo to a dozen smaller ships equipped for high speed runs to the more remote work sites in the region. I see a lot of profit in your future, {[character]player.name}, if you stick with us.

There are few things I despise more than a quitter. If you come back to my station I am sure we can find you a position on the station slave labor gang, scrubbing the personal hygiene tanks with a toothbrush for the next six months.

History has shown us that a properly motivated slave work force can work harder and longer - especially in harsh conditions - if they are provided the means to enhance their everyday lives. Well, for many decades, the provision of various stimulant drugs to slave laborers was considered a standard method of doing business. However, the downside to this was that, while the use of stims typically increased productivity, more often than not it resulted in significant long term health problems for the slaves leading to shortened lifespans and, more importantly, to decreased profits. So, while the use of stimulants has largely been discontinued, the idea that drugs could increase slave output never entirely went away, though it did require a new approach.

To this end, my company recently developed an inexpensive new drug that works on the pleasure centers of the brain, providing what we might call a “reward” for hard work. Importantly, this drug, known as Blue Paradise, or "Beep" as the techs call it, has been proven in real-world testing to increase slave labor output by as much as twenty percent across the board, without any known long term health problems. As you can guess, the increased profit potential here is, well, staggering. Equally important is the fact that we have not reported this new drug to the various control boards; nor do we intend to at this juncture.

We need you to deliver a very large shipment of this drug to a forward logistics hub station from which it will be transshipped to ore mines, agricultural farms, and other slave-intensive operations. I can give you my guarantee that this cargo will not be flagged by customs or the police, as it is not yet deemed an illegal substance.

So, can we count on you to deliver this?
Good, glad to hear it. I will immediately order the refrigerated secure containers moved into your cargo hold for your prompt departure.

We all know that there have been a long series of proclamations, laws, and rules banning the transportation of illegal drugs (and some legal drugs) in Amarr space for use in slave labor. These prohibitions have typically had no real teeth, unless of course the Empress herself sets forth an official decree specifically banning a given substance. The logical, time-tested way around this has been to create entirely new generations of performance enhancing biochemical drugs.

As slaves are typically wary of any pills or other obvious means of altering their behavior (recalling, as we must, the various slave uprisings that have occurred when we tried to openly force drugs on them), we've had to resort to less obvious methods. For example, we have surreptitiously and gradually delivered the drugs into laborer's systems through aerosols in their habitat ventilation systems, impregnated substances into their foodstuffs and water supplies, and other rather clever means, I won't go into here. What is important is that the result has almost always been a positive one, with significant increases in worker productivity.

The downside to this, however, has been a decline in overall slave lifespans due to the long term effects of these drugs. Normally, this would be considered simple attrition; a cost of doing businesses. However, as it continues to become more and more difficult to obtain new slaves (particularly given the intolerable and unjust interference of the other empires), this solution is less and less viable. We need them to live as long as possible. This reality, of course, leads us to the only other benign option – drugs as a part of a rewards system for those slaves who meet a certain work quota each day.

To this end, we shall continue to develop new substances to both avoid interference by Customs and police forces and to ensure the maximum possible output by our slave laborers.

I'm sure you're all too aware of our war with the Caldari State. It's been dragging on for years with no end in sight... until now, that is. We've been making some good headway on the active front and our research and development has been busy behind the scenes. Military scientists have developed a hybrid round that works like single-target burst ECM, and it's time to introduce it to the military for an active field-test.

Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
Do not fail us, {[character]player.name}. The Federation is depending on you.
I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought your loyalty might mean more to you.
I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. If we find that you've shared this with the Caldari, it will not go well for you.
Have you finished your delivery, {[character]player.name}?
Thank you, {[character]player.name}. You are a true child of the Federation.
Electronic Counter-Countermeasures

There has always been contention over the effectiveness of the Federation's sensor-dampening ewar tactics against the State's ECM. Some military scientists feel that, in adding ECM to the hybrid arsenal, the Federation would be admitting to a weakness and confirming the State's superiority; others argue that turning the enemy's tactics against them is an essential facet of wartime, and that rejecting the opportunity is effectively signing off on the Federation's defeat. The debate rages in both the staterooms and the laboratories even as research and development continues.
Excellent news, pilot, thank you for updating us as to your position and condition. Please make all possible speed to the destination so that we can then dispatch the combined rescue team package.

We've received confirmation that you did indeed fulfill your promise and deliver the Marines to the station. As we speak, the combined rescue team is loading into other ship for immediate transport to the Harbinger. Hopefully, we will reach them in time.

Quitting? Now?  You have placed our marines and hundreds of other personnel in grave danger by abandoning them mid-mission. We will have to find some way to get them to our damaged strategic cruiser, though I feel it is now too late.
We will not forget this – the moment you chose to abandon our people in a time of great need. Your assistance could have turned the tide of this whole disaster. Do not contact me again.
I have to request a difficult task of you: play nice with a swarm of Angel Cartel representatives and their entourage on your ship. Hopefully they won't try to cause you trouble.

This is a list of people I want you to escort to a meeting. They have quite a large security entourage, and as you can see from some of the names, they have a reason for it. These people are members of the Angel Cartel. While the Cartel are thugs and pirate scum, and are not particularly welcome in Minmatar space, it does not mean that some corporations don't have certain dealings with them.

This isn't your usual business meeting this time, however. Evidently, the Cartel overstepped their bounds, and the corporation took it to the Republic. Escort these Angel representatives to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; we'll take care of the rest. For the sake of appearances, try to treat them politely. We don't want them to know it's a set-up until they get to the boardroom.
Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Please hurry.
I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}, but I can understand why you might decline.
I'm extremely disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
Hello, {[character]player.name}. Have you finished your work for me?
Excellent, thank you, {[character]player.name}. I think we got our point across to them; there are some things you do not try to push in the Republic.
Borderland Outlaws

The Angel Cartel's reputation for engaging in any activity regardless of its legality has earned it the DED's description of the most dangerous criminal organization in the cluster. With a corporate command structure and open recruitment policy, the Cartel are less thugs than sharks in pinstripe suits, capable of operating on all levels of society. With a major operational base in Etherium Reach on the edge of Minmatar space, the Cartel is held with deep suspicion within the Republic. Their annexation of the Skarkon system in YC 110 and sudden withdrawal left many unanswered questions regarding both the Cartel's intentions towards the Republic and what deals were forged under the table to make them leave... and what those deals might have cost.

A short time ago, Minmatar terrorists in a combined fleet of frigates and cruisers attacked one of our Harbinger-class strategic cruisers as it was transporting slaves from a recently closed mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in a nearby system. While all but one of the attackers was annihilated, our convoy's escorts were destroyed and our cruiser is burning. Making a bad situation worse, we are anticipating that the terrorists will return in force within the next several hours to attempt the theft of our slaves, as they almost certainly know the cruiser is alone and all but helpless.

Our concern is that if the terrorists feel that they have a window of opportunity to recover these slaves, it is likely that they will throw everything they have into the effort. Our intelligence assessments of the terrorists' fleet assets are even less reassuring: we believe that they could send as many as four battlecruisers into this fight – more than enough to wipe out the arriving frigates and forcefully board our heavily damaged strategic cruiser. However, we have calculated that if we can delay any terrorist boarding parties long enough, this should give us enough time for the much larger main rescue fleet to arrive.

The only bright side to this situation, in what is unquestionably an act of divine providence, is that a large contingent of marines are aboard this station as we speak, having just completed specialized refresher training in counter-boarding operations. We need you to deliver them to the station closest to the last reported position of our cruiser. From there, we will transport a combined team of marines, engineers, medics, and other essential personnel to hopefully stop the fire and save the ship - along with its cargo of highly valuable slaves. However, this mission must be undertaken immediately. Any delay will surely doom the Harbinger and her brave crew.

Our deepest thanks for taking on this mission. I can tell you that our best analysts feel that you should be fairly safe in this mission, as the terrorist will have to focus all their efforts on targeting the stricken cruiser. They simply won't have the ships or the time to even attempt to interdict your ship as you make your way to the destination station.
What? Who doesn't want to take advantage of anti-tech crazies?
Well, fine. But burn the holos. We don't want normal people watching that stuff.
The Altered Generations

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is hosting a fashion show for publicity, and your agent needs you to pick up the models. For some reason, they think you won't get fed up and drop them all off in orbit around the nearest moon.

The Federal Talent Showcase is upon us, that time of year where all the artists and “artists” come out of hiding and shove the products of the past year in our faces. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is playing host to a fashion show and we need someone to pick up the models and fashionistas from {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. You can kind of guess what they're like – a normal pilot just isn't good enough for them, so I have to find a capsuleer I think is level-headed enough to not vent cargo into space if they get too annoying. I know you can handle it, it's not like you have to speak with them face to face, anyway.
Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I'll make it worth your while.
Regrettable, but I can't say I blame you, {[character]player.name}.
I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. We have a reputation to maintain.
Have you picked up the models yet? The show's only a few hours away!
Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I imagine you're happy to have that lot off your hands.
Gallente Haute Couture

In a culture as materialistic and appearance-conscious as the Gallente, the ability to stay on the bleeding edge is a valuable asset. “Clothes,” fashion critic Marko Envaumier said in a well-known interview with the Scope, “are an outward expression of man's inner nature and outlook toward life. Professional secretaries study fashion alongside the other office skills ... to learn to gauge the worth of both potential clients and employees for the companies that hire them. Next time you walk into an office, remember that the boy or girl behind the desk is checking your tailoring.”

We have recently been experiencing an increase in terrorist attacks by groups seeking to free Amarr slaves in this region. Their raids have become more complex and lethal, resulting in the loss of untold millions of ISK worth of valuable property. More importantly, one of the regional governors is having his annual gala event at his estate on a nearby planet. We need you to deliver a cargo of elite conditioned slaves to a station we will designate. From there they will be transported to the governor's estate by heavily armed ships.

You are aware, no doubt, of the rumors of extremist antislavery terrorist groups within the Amarr Empire itself. Well, you know then that their loyalty to the Empire is indeed secondary to their overarching desire to see all slaves freed and made equal members of society. This is a condition that we, as the greatest state in all of New Eden, simply cannot tolerate. However, our efforts at arresting and reeducating those insurgents have largely failed to permanently change the mindsets of these rather fanatical individuals.

This system has been particularly hard hit by this and other like-minded groups.
