Therefore, we need you to rescue this team immediately and bring them back to us for an emergency debriefing and to ensure their safety.

After running a check of qualified pilots in our office database, your name was near the top of the list. We estimate there will only be sufficient time for this one rescue attempt before the assassins strike.
Caldari SIGINT Outpost Network

The Caldari Navy, much like the military services of other races, operates a covert network of signals intelligence outposts along the borders of the Caldari State. The specific, primary mission of these stations is to provide advance early warning of any hostile incursion by the Gallente military. Beyond this vital mission, however, the outposts are also tasked with gathering intelligence on a wide variety of other targets, both military and civilian. Of particular interest is the regular provision of information on the movement of the commercial and industrial fleets of other races, given the competition between the Caldari corporate system and foreign companies. In this way, the outposts not only provide an essential early warning system for any hostile forces, but also provide data of immense economic value, thus better enabling the Caldari private business sector to better compete in the merciless realm of interstellar business.

There is no time to discuss this mission further given the haste with which you will need to accomplish this. Please contact me only when you have delivered the contractors safely to the final destination.
Thank you for agreeing to attempt the rescue of our civilian contractors. You must leave very soon if we are to have any hope of reaching them before the hit team arrives.

Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. During a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's sensor cross-section, making it much easier to detect and attack. Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Therefore, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet.

Greetings, {[character]player.name}. Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. He swallowed a hidden poison tablet as we moved in to arrest him, so he is no longer a threat.

However, during a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's signature radius, making it much easier for our enemies to detect and attack.

Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Essentially, the Widow's commander would not know that his ship had lost its critical operational advantage until he was detected and targeted by hostile combatants. Given the very specialized role of this ship, not only would the Widow be compromised, but it is possible than any ships he might be bridging in via its covert jump portal generator could be unknowingly hot dropped near a waiting enemy fleet, instead of empty space.

In order to remedy this critical situation, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet. This shipment represents our best and only hope to quickly repair the damage done by the Gallente spy and ensure the safety of our brave Widow pilots and crew.
Do not contact me on an open channel until this mission is complete. Remember, this is a clandestine operation!
Your successful delivery of the prototype nanites will undoubtedly save the lives of many Black Ops pilots and crew. You have the makings of a good counter operative!
We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our Black Ops teams at great risk. We will have to find another operative elsewhere.
We are disappointed that you've chosen not to accept this critical mission. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere.

Produced by the Kaalakiota megacorporation, the Widow-class Black Ops battleship represents the current edge technology for Caldari military vessels used in covert operations. The primary function of the Widow is to conduct infiltration and espionage behind enemy lines. Specifically, when equipped with covert cynosural field generators and covert jump portal generators, the ship can create a “bridge” through which conventional ships are instantly transported, much like a jump gate. The effect of this is to surprise an enemy by instantly “hot dropping” a combat fleet into what was, moments prior, only empty space. In addition, it can also be fitted with ECM modules and cruise missiles such that it can provide jamming capabilities and supporting firepower if necessary. Using this technology, the Widow represents a significant force multiplier in the ongoing conflicts faced by the Caldari State.
We are relieved to hear that you've accepted this important mission. It is imperative that you deliver this cargo with all possible haste.
Widow-class Black Ops Battleships

A team of mercenaries led by a man calling himself “Black Dog” has killed one of our senior managers as he toured an asteroid field not far from here. Intelligence has indicated that he intends to continue these operations into the foreseeable future. To remedy this unacceptable situation, we need you to transport a trained assassin and his entourage to a station closer to the scene of the crime. Once this is done, you will have completed the terms of this contract. We appreciate your discretion in this endeavor.
Corporate Assassins
We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our executives and even our miners at significant risk from these mercenaries.

Your unwillingness to assist us in this matter is going to cost this corporation a great deal of isk until we can find some other way to resolve it. Mr. Smith may soon take a personal interest in you, as you've now disrupted his lucrative contract. I certainly don't want to be in your shoes once he gets the word.

We all know the saying, “business is war.” Nowhere is this adage practiced more seriously than in the Caldari corporate world. The soldiers in this fight are typically thought of as the salesmen, managers, executives, and other boardroom warriors. However, from time to time a very special skill set is required to deal with an equally specific threat. For these situations, corporate assassins are sometimes required to resolve issues that cannot be otherwise remedied through conventional channels. In the most extreme cases, these highly-trained operatives, most of whom served particularly arduous and dangerous careers in the Caldari Special Forces and intelligence groups, are hired to carry out very selective missions with very limited goals. The missions they are paid, - highly paid at that - to undertake would rival any holovid espionage movie, though the consequences are, of course, much more serious. You don't want to mess with these guys, and gals, as it is usually the last thing you'll ever do.

We just received word from Mr. Smith that you did indeed deliver him on time and without attracting any unusual inquiries. We hope the compensation for this mission was worth your time. The Caldari State can use more competent and discretionary pilots like you.
Why are you contacting me?

Before we begin, I must make one thing perfectly clear: You were never here, and this meeting never took place. You do understand what I mean, yes?

We are in need of a pilot who can deliver a very sensitive cargo from this station to a nearby station, without attracting any undue attention. You may have heard in the news or the local gossip channels that a Caldari regional director for mining operations was murdered yesterday by unknown assailants while touring an asteroid field in his personal shuttle. That much is indeed true. However, what has not been reported is that we have, in the last few hours, learned the identity of the assassin, a mercenary who goes by the name “Black Dog”, and that he and his team have already begun to plan for an ongoing hit-and-run campaign designed to try and scare off Caldari corporations from any future mining activities in the region.

Of course, we cannot allow this kind of disruption to what has proven a highly lucrative endeavor – the Board and our shareholders simply will not tolerate any further dips in revenues. To remedy this interruption, one of our sister companies that specializes in, shall we say, discrete solutions, has loaned us one of their most highly trained specialists to resolve this issue. His name, as you might expect, is Mr. Smith. His mission, in brief, is to liquidate Black Dog, along with any associates that may be operating with him at the time.

What we need from you, and need soon, is for you to transport Mr. Smith and his entourage to a station closer to the action – one with a hangar walkway the leads directly to an unmarked office. Once you have dropped him off, your role in this action will be complete.

So, what is it going to be, pilot? We need a yes or no right now if this operation is to stay on schedule.

In order to get around the laws pertaining to the transportation of illegal drugs through Amarr Empire space, we have been forced to create new and unknown substances for use on, or by, rather, our various slave labor enclaves. This new drug, Blue Paradise, does away with many of the harmful chemicals previously used while actually increasing the pleasurable effects. We are certain that, properly controlled and distributed, introduction of this drug into the slave labor workforce will increase productivity by a substantial margin. We are counting on you to deliver it to the designation transshipment station as soon as possible.
Biochemical Agents for Improved Slave Workloads
Well, you have certainly wasted my very valuable time. I thought we could count on you, but obviously I was misinformed. Don't count on working for me any time soon.

Excellent. We are transferring your cargo to a dozen smaller ships equipped for high speed runs to the more remote work sites in the region. I see a lot of profit in your future, {[character]player.name}, if you stick with us.

There are few things I despise more than a quitter. If you come back to my station I am sure we can find you a position on the station slave labor gang, scrubbing the personal hygiene tanks with a toothbrush for the next six months.

History has shown us that a properly motivated slave work force can work harder and longer - especially in harsh conditions - if they are provided the means to enhance their everyday lives. Well, for many decades, the provision of various stimulant drugs to slave laborers was considered a standard method of doing business. However, the downside to this was that, while the use of stims typically increased productivity, more often than not it resulted in significant long term health problems for the slaves leading to shortened lifespans and, more importantly, to decreased profits. So, while the use of stimulants has largely been discontinued, the idea that drugs could increase slave output never entirely went away, though it did require a new approach.

To this end, my company recently developed an inexpensive new drug that works on the pleasure centers of the brain, providing what we might call a “reward” for hard work. Importantly, this drug, known as Blue Paradise, or "Beep" as the techs call it, has been proven in real-world testing to increase slave labor output by as much as twenty percent across the board, without any known long term health problems. As you can guess, the increased profit potential here is, well, staggering. Equally important is the fact that we have not reported this new drug to the various control boards; nor do we intend to at this juncture.

We need you to deliver a very large shipment of this drug to a forward logistics hub station from which it will be transshipped to ore mines, agricultural farms, and other slave-intensive operations. I can give you my guarantee that this cargo will not be flagged by customs or the police, as it is not yet deemed an illegal substance.

So, can we count on you to deliver this?
Good, glad to hear it. I will immediately order the refrigerated secure containers moved into your cargo hold for your prompt departure.

We all know that there have been a long series of proclamations, laws, and rules banning the transportation of illegal drugs (and some legal drugs) in Amarr space for use in slave labor. These prohibitions have typically had no real teeth, unless of course the Empress herself sets forth an official decree specifically banning a given substance. The logical, time-tested way around this has been to create entirely new generations of performance enhancing biochemical drugs.

As slaves are typically wary of any pills or other obvious means of altering their behavior (recalling, as we must, the various slave uprisings that have occurred when we tried to openly force drugs on them), we've had to resort to less obvious methods. For example, we have surreptitiously and gradually delivered the drugs into laborer's systems through aerosols in their habitat ventilation systems, impregnated substances into their foodstuffs and water supplies, and other rather clever means, I won't go into here. What is important is that the result has almost always been a positive one, with significant increases in worker productivity.

The downside to this, however, has been a decline in overall slave lifespans due to the long term effects of these drugs. Normally, this would be considered simple attrition; a cost of doing businesses. However, as it continues to become more and more difficult to obtain new slaves (particularly given the intolerable and unjust interference of the other empires), this solution is less and less viable. We need them to live as long as possible. This reality, of course, leads us to the only other benign option – drugs as a part of a rewards system for those slaves who meet a certain work quota each day.

To this end, we shall continue to develop new substances to both avoid interference by Customs and police forces and to ensure the maximum possible output by our slave laborers.
We know the mission is proceeding well, as we've got a cloaked Covert Ops ship following you at a discrete distance. Please contact me only in the event of an emergency.
I'm glad to hear you're going to help us out here. We aren't expecting any trouble with this one, but with corporate espionage, you never know – keep your eyes open.

By quitting mid-mission you've singlehandedly compromised the whole operation! I doubt we'll be able to flush out the spy now, given the fact that you've interrupted the shipment – no doubt he will sense something is up and simply remain unknown to us.
Well, we are disappointed that you've turned this one down. We'll have to use one of our own transportation pilots to get this done.

Outstanding job, {[character]player.name}! As you may have heard by now, the spy was caught trying to remove the device from the offload cargo bay on the station. Needless to say, he has a very uncomfortable future ahead of him in one of our interrogation facilities. Thanks to your piloting skills and discretion, our work on the new cloak remains a well guarded secret.

We have reason to believe that a small team of Gallente saboteurs has managed to destroy one of our new – and not yet fully operational – Command Centers on a nearby ice planet. These facilities are critical elements in our overall plan to dominate the planet such that we can then exploit the vast and lucrative materials that we have identified there in abundance. We need you to deliver a large complement of Arctic Warfare Marines to a forward station so that they can then be transferred down to provide the security we so desperately need. Their massive amounts of equipment will be brought in on other ships, so we need you to deliver these men safely and securely – everything depends on their safe arrival.
Need to Know
Are the Marines behaving themselves? Good. Please continue to make all possible haste in delivering them to the station. They tend to get a bit rowdy when they are cooped up too long.

How you can quit this mission mid-stream is absolutely beyond me. Do you have any idea the mountains of isk that this is going to cause my department and the Planetary Exploitation Division as a whole? Don't ever come back here for a while.

I'm glad to you hear that you've agreed to help us out on this one. If you'll just confirm this manifest, we'll rally the Marines and have them report to your ship immediately. You'd better get moving – don't want to keep the troops waiting.

We have so far managed to keep this event a closely held secret, as we do not want to discourage the senior management of the company from further exploiting the extremely valuable materials that are in largely untapped abundance on the sea floor. If word of this was to get out at this critical stage, it might give them reason pack up and move to a safer location - perhaps even to another planet. Well, this would simply be unacceptable, as our new planetary industry efforts have so far generated record revenues - the one thing keeping our shareholders and investors happy. And we want to keep them happy, if you understand my meaning. We must allow nothing to interrupt that flow of ISK into our corporate coffers.

I just got word that you delivered all the Marines safely to the station, great job! However, I must now coordinate the follow-on shipment of their equipment and weapons, which is going to mean another all-nighter here at the office. Oh well, business first, yes?  We will be in touch for future missions, so thanks again.

That you have chosen to decline this mission has put this company in a very difficult position, to say the least. Well, get out of here then; let us hope the Marines don't hear about this and decide to give you a rather rough send-off.

Two days ago, a covert Gallente strike team infiltrated and destroyed a brand new Command Center on a nearby ice planet. We think they managed to infiltrate as local civilian workers due the fact that the facility's Personnel Security Identification Systems had not yet been fully brought online. This unforgivable lapse in security enabled the four-man team to gain access to a highly secure area that contains the controls for the counter-harmonic stabilizers which, in short, keep the entire facility level and secure in the very harsh climates encountered on that planet. A series of well-placed explosives damaged these stabilizers, however, taking them offline and causing the entire command center to collapse and sink through the ice to the ocean floor some two kilometers below. Fortunately, the bulk of the work force was not scheduled to arrive for two more weeks, so casualties were very light. The financial and economic costs were, however, staggering.

Now that you understand the gravity of the situation, we can proceed to the reason that we contacted you to help us in this critical moment in the company's ongoing rapid expansion phase. We need you to very quietly transport a company of our best Arctic Warfare Marines from this station to the destination station with all possible haste. From there they will flown to the ice planet to provide a very high level of security for this and other nearby command centers and facilities. It is just a matter of time before this disastrous event becomes public knowledge, and we need to prove to the senior management, shareholders, and investors that we have the security situation resolutely in hand.

So, {[character]player.name}, are you willing to help us out by delivering a large number of Arctic Marines to the designated station?

During a high-level security assessment, a decoy maglev train designed to mimic the regional governor's chartered train was destroyed by unknown saboteurs while traveling at very high speed. Our investigation has yet to uncover the traitors; however, we are confident that a prompt scientific examination of the wreckage will provide the clues we need to resolve this internal security matter. We are sending a team of senior investigators to the wreck site so that they might help determine the identities of the attackers. We are counting on you to fly them to the designated station.

I know the security screening process at this station has been time-consuming and a bit, well, intrusive. Now that you have passed our various tests, however, I feel confident that I can now let you in on the reason you are here.

One of our regional governors had recently been planning an unannounced visit to one of the new planetary command centers in a nearby system. For security reasons, this information was restricted to only those in the governor's inner circle, to include the commander of his personal security detail. Well, this commander decided to test his internal security prior to this event, to best ensure the governor's safe travel. So, for this exercise, he created a painstakingly detailed agenda, identical in every detail to an actual state visit. In this scenario, the governor was to travel by chartered high-speed maglev train to a number of the new planetary command centers.

As the Governor's decoy train traveled through a large canyon, however, a series of explosive charges detonated on the rail line, sending the train off its track and into the canyon wall. As it turned out, the security commander's ruse had worked perfectly; someone in the governor's inner circle had tipped his or her hand and provided information to unknown assassins.

So far, however, we have not been able to determine the traitor's identity, and each member of the inner circle is vehemently denying any involvement, despite our best chemical interrogations. So, what this investigation will likely boil down to is to what clues can be solved from the train wreckage, the destroyed maglev track sections, and the soil around the site of the blasts.

We need you to transport several investigative teams, along with a considerable amount of equipment, to a nearby station where they will then be transported via shuttle to the planet. Will you take on this mission?
Thank you for agreeing to aid the Empire in this matter. My assistant will provide you all the details you will need to deliver these personnel to the designated station.
We are extremely disappointed in your decision to leave this mission. I am quite sure the Regional Governor's office will not soon forget this offense to the Empire.

We are disappointed in your decision not to assist the Empire in its hour of need. However, we do have another pilot waiting in the next room, so you may leave. And I need not remind you of the consequences should you discuss any of what you have been told here today.

Excellent work, pilot. The personnel you transported for us have already developed some interesting leads, and it seems – at least at this early juncture – that the assassins may be of Minmatar descent. Further testing, we expect, will confirm this. We will retain your contact information, should this incident require more of your courier skills.

Thank you a million times over, pilot, for taking on this mission. The hearts and minds of the Amarr faithful in that station and elsewhere will benefit immeasurably from your prompt delivery of these hallowed holoreels.

Well, I was not expecting this. All we needed was for you to make a simple run from this station to the designated station and drop off our cargo. Well, suffice to say, you will not be receiving any prayers of blessing from me tonight!
Our hearts are glad to know that you are en route to the station and will be docking there shortly. Please contact me on arrival.

While transporting Minmatar slaves from a recently close ore mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in nearby system, the convoy was attacked by terrorists, destroying the escort frigates and heavily damaging the Harbinger-class strategic cruiser carrying the slaves. We believe it is likely that the terrorists will return, and in larger ships, to attempt a rescue of the slaves before we can respond with reinforcements. The window of opportunity for the terrorists is short, so it is imperative that we immediately render as much help as possible. What we need you to do is deliver a contingent of heavily armed marines recently trained in counter-boarding operations to a station closer to the site of the battle. From there, they will join other Amarr military and rescue teams for immediate transportation to the damaged cruiser.
Excellent news, pilot, thank you for updating us as to your position and condition. Please make all possible speed to the destination so that we can then dispatch the combined rescue team package.

We've received confirmation that you did indeed fulfill your promise and deliver the Marines to the station. As we speak, the combined rescue team is loading into other ship for immediate transport to the Harbinger. Hopefully, we will reach them in time.

Quitting? Now?  You have placed our marines and hundreds of other personnel in grave danger by abandoning them mid-mission. We will have to find some way to get them to our damaged strategic cruiser, though I feel it is now too late.
We will not forget this – the moment you chose to abandon our people in a time of great need. Your assistance could have turned the tide of this whole disaster. Do not contact me again.

Our deepest thanks for taking on this mission. I can tell you that our best analysts feel that you should be fairly safe in this mission, as the terrorist will have to focus all their efforts on targeting the stricken cruiser. They simply won't have the ships or the time to even attempt to interdict your ship as you make your way to the destination station.

We have recently been experiencing an increase in terrorist attacks by groups seeking to free Amarr slaves in this region. Their raids have become more complex and lethal, resulting in the loss of untold millions of ISK worth of valuable property. More importantly, one of the regional governors is having his annual gala event at his estate on a nearby planet. We need you to deliver a cargo of elite conditioned slaves to a station we will designate. From there they will be transported to the governor's estate by heavily armed ships.

You are aware, no doubt, of the rumors of extremist antislavery terrorist groups within the Amarr Empire itself. Well, you know then that their loyalty to the Empire is indeed secondary to their overarching desire to see all slaves freed and made equal members of society. This is a condition that we, as the greatest state in all of New Eden, simply cannot tolerate. However, our efforts at arresting and reeducating those insurgents have largely failed to permanently change the mindsets of these rather fanatical individuals.

This system has been particularly hard hit by this and other like-minded groups. Most recently, an Anathema-class covert ops ship, specially configured to transport elite slaves to the estates of senior Amarr leaders in the region, was somehow decloaked, its weapons and sensors jammed, and ruthlessly attacked to the point of near-total structure failure. The terrorists then demanded the pilot transfer the slaves to this mystery ship, on threat of the total destruction of the covert ops vessel. The pilot complied, though he has since been punished for his cowardice.

It is for this reason that I called you here today. I need you to transport a new shipment of elite slaves to a nearby station for further transshipment to the residence of one of the regional governors. This shipment is of particular urgency as the governor is hosting his annual gala event at his estate, and the usual staff of slaves simply will not do. We need these specific slaves, as they have been trained in protocol, proper food and drink service, entertainment, and numerous other talents that I need not mention here.

Will you take on this courier mission on behalf of the Empire and deliver these highly trained and extremely expensive slaves to the designated station?
Amarr Anti-Slavery Terrorist Groups

While it might seem impossible at first glance, there are indeed small bands of terrorists who seek to upset the very core foundation of our society by working to eliminate slavery throughout the Empire. We have had significant success in disrupting these groups, with many members killed or taken prisoner. Nonetheless, like a hydra they continue to grow and adapt to our tactics and operations, making them a quite annoying thorn in our side. The Amarr Empire is devoting increasing resources to the eradication of these groups; however, even the most optimistic analysts concede that it may be quite some time before this nascent insurgency can be eradicated.

Thank you for the update pilot, it is rather reassuring that you are flying without any interference from our unwanted friends. Please contact me again when you are being towed in to the dock, as only then will I feel assured that this courier mission was a success.

You must be kidding?!? I have already guaranteed the governor's office that you are en route and will arrive at the scheduled time. This act on your part is probably going to get me reassigned to some asteroid in an uncharted system a million light years from here. Well, I will make sure I'm not the only one who will feel the heat for this failure.

While I must say I am rather shocked at your refusal to undertake this mission, we are fortunate in that we do have contingency plans in place. So, while we will have to risk the crew and slaves in another run, I feel confident that only you will bear the negative feedback for failing us here today.
Great job, {[character]player.name}. The slaves are being offloaded now and will be en route to the governor's estate shortly. I can't thank you enough for your reliability and promptness.
That is very good news, pilot. I will contact the governor's aide myself to let her know that you have accepted and will be departing shortly.

Suicide terrorists have been attacking and destroying our commercial convoys as they have passed through their usual transit zones, despite the presence of heavy security escort vessels. A communications intercept, partially decoded, indicates that these individual intend to step up the level of their attacks by targeting the stations themselves. While we can defend against some of these attackers, based on analysis of their previous attack profiles, we have never had to defend against pilots and ships who fully intend to die by throwing themselves against us without regard for their own lives. Tactical analysis indicates that they will get through our defense and may cause catastrophic damage, likely killing hundreds if not thousands of our civilian workforce and their families. We need you to help us evacuate them immediately!

We have virtually no information on these new threats, other than that they have access to very fast ships filled to the brim with high explosives. Their tactics are simple – they seem to appear out of nowhere, then accelerate their ships to maximum velocity and, ignoring defensive fire, fly directly into the cargo bays of our freighters and other haulers. We are currently working with Caldari Naval Intelligence to determine the source of this scourge; however, early indications from their ship markings are that they belong to an extremists environmental cult that views the Caldari State as the ultimate evil in the universe. They will stop at nothing to destroy us, especially as we expand planetary industry and resource harvesting.

You are quitting on us now? In the middle of an evacuation? Fine. Just deliver those men, women, and children to the nearest safe location, and we will send someone to get them. You are a despicable coward and you'd better hope you never need to transit through this system ever again.

I will never be able to thank you for helping us in our most dire hour. The Caldari Navy should be arriving soon to provide additional security, but that's no guarantee that the terrorists won't follow through with their insidious plans. I will be sure to pass the word throughout the comms networks of the great service you did for all of us today.
I cannot believe what I'm hearing – you are refusing to help save these people? Well, I don't know where we are going to find another ship at this late hour.
Thank you. That is a big load off my shoulders. We need all the good pilots we can get to help us get these people to safety before the terrorists attempt any suicide attack against this station.

Thank you for the update. I am glad to hear the passengers are doing well. I can't tell you how much it means to us that you are willing to divert from more profitable ventures to save these innocent lives.
Anti-Caldari Suicide Terrorists

There's a fitness initiative going through Federation schools. I'm sure you've heard about it? A weird luddite group called The Natural Way wants to get kids to stop relying on modding to stay in shape, and they're tossing cred around like water to do so. No school would turn down money in exchange for a couple hours' fitness classes a week. Take these {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} over to one of their facilities at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll see some of that money, too.

There's a fitness initiative going through Federation schools. I'm sure you've heard about it? A weird luddite group called The Natural Way wants to get kids to stop relying on modding to stay in shape, and they're tossing cred around like water to do so. No school would turn down money in exchange for a couple hours' fitness classes a week. Take these {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} over to one of their facilities at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll see some of that money, too.

The Natural Way is a group which promotes a lower-tech way of life. They're throwing around a lot of cred to start a fitness initiative encouraging kids to stay away from body modding, and I see nothing wrong with encouraging them in exchange for a little ISK.

Body modification, or "modding," is widely accepted throughout the Federation, primarily for cosmetic purposes. Color-changing tattoos which move, programmable "makeup" which is implanted in subcutaneous layers, piercings and body-shaping are the most common forms, so normal they're barely worth mentioning. The wilder forms of modding, however, can frequently give people the wrong idea. Parents who want to discourage their children from engaging in extreme modding may sometimes turn to groups which support lower-tech ways of life for educational programs, particularly in the tumultuous teenage years when youngsters start to seek their personal identity.
Just don't watch those, okay? They gave me nightmares.
You haven't WATCHED those, have you?
Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. My mother's been giving those to my kids for their birthdays every year, and I was afraid I'd never get rid of them.
Trust me, pilot, we are watching you, and we know you are on time and flying via the preprogrammed waypoints. Contact us only on your arrival.
Trust me, pilot, we are watching you, and we know you are on time and flying via the preprogrammed waypoints. Contact us only on your arrival.

Looks like food supplies are dwindling fast at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I think people are consuming a lot more than they were before. Take them a shipment of frozen food so we can feed the hungry.

Looks like there was some kind of explosion on a colony in this system, and thousands of people are without a home. I want you to take some of them over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can do our part in providing shelter for less fortunate people.

Looks like there was some kind of explosion on a colony in this system, and thousands of people are without a home. I want you to take some of them over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can do our part in providing shelter for less fortunate people.

We have received word that the extraction team has taken delivery of your cargo and is now en route to the planet. Given the speed with which you delivered this essential shipment, we assess a high likelihood that the stranded team will be safely extracted. Well done!

We have received word that the extraction team has taken delivery of your cargo and is now en route to the planet. Given the speed with which you delivered this essential shipment, we assess a high likelihood that the stranded team will be safely extracted. Well done!

As you know, there are many hundreds of thousands of Minmatar slaves working to provide essential services to the Empire, just as they have for centuries. Given their considerable natural physical abilities, they have always made up one of the most important and valuable ethnic groups within the vast Amarr slave workforce. One unavoidable consequence of this, however, is that we have had to invest a considerable amount of money, not only in the health and welfare of these slaves, but also to ensure their obedience.

One important aspect of this latter effort has been the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRC's, which are designed to house some of the more problematic slaves in order to facilitate their eventual return to the workforce. In recent months, however, there has been a significant increase in violent disobedience at certain LRC's, with some of the more severe instances leading to near-riots.

Our immediate problem is that one of these facilities, LRC-12A, has been taken over during just such an uprising. The slaves have reportedly killed and injured dozens of our personnel and taken the remainder hostage. They are demanding the immediate release of their fellow slaves at a nearby Amarr mining operation, along with transportation to a destination of their choosing. We have, so far, managed to keep this incident quiet; if the Minmatar Republic leadership were to learn of this, it could very easily lead to much more severe consequences for both races. The only way to ensure this does not happen is through the immediate application of overwhelming force.

Therefore, we need you to deliver a large contingent of specially trained Riot Interdiction Teams to a nearby station, from which they will join up with other security elements for final transportation to LRC-12A. Will you assist us?
The teams have begun to embark on a small fleet of frigates and cruisers for LRC-12A. With this amount of men and lethal weaponry, there is no doubt that we shall prevail!

Our engineering scientists, working at our highly secure, clandestine R&D facility on a nearby planet have produced a new type of cloaking device that, when fitted to Covert Ops ships, could theoretically enable them to jump through stargates without uncloaking! And yes, I can see by the look on your face that you must think I've had far too many Extra Strength Quafe sodas today. However, I can assure you that, while it may be many years before this technology is perfected and suitable for even experimental use, the science behind it is quite real, and this is where this story takes a very important twist.

Our internal security teams have managed to uncover a plan formulated by one of our competitors to steal the prototype cloaking system at some point between the time it leaves the lab up until it arrives at the field testing facility over in the next system. Problem is, we don't yet know who the spy is, so we devised a plan to get that spy to expose himself so that we can then move in and make the arrest.

To this end, you will be delivering is a very detailed mock-up series of the actual prototype, one that will withstand an initial visual and electronic scrutiny on the part of the thief. In all practical terms, however, these devices could no more cloak a ship than it could cook your morning breakfast. We are naming this event Operation Doorstop, which is our planning team's attempt at humor, given the uselessness of this particular lump of metal and wires. What we do need, though, is your absolute confidentiality on this shipment. If the spy gets any whiff that this is a set-up, we will likely never know who he or she is, and we will remain at ongoing risk of one of our most important R&D projects potentially falling into the wrong hands.

So, what do you say, {[character]player.name}? Willing to take on this rather interesting assignment?

However, it has recently been brought to our attention that a corporate espionage agent sent by a rival company is targeting this new technology, for obvious reasons. In order to flush him out and arrest him, however, we need to catch him in the act. So, we are asking you to transport a decoy prototype cloaking device from this station to one we designate. With such a juicy target, we feel the spy will not be able to resist making an attempt to steal is somewhere between here and there. We need you to fly this device to that station utilizing absolute secrecy.
That is very good news, thank you. With your permission, we will begin loading pallets of the Ditanium plates into your hangar.

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s R&D branch has been working on more efficient version of the inertial compensator units used in starship propulsion systems. I need you to take the latest batch to the testing facility.
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s R&D branch has been working on a more efficient version of Carbon-86 epoxy resin. I need you to take the latest batch to the testing facility.

Federation R&D specialists have been working to find counters for Caldari military tactics; the latest development is a special type of ammunition that works similarly to a lock breaker bomb, but on a single target. I want you to take it over to a navy base for testing, and you need to keep word of this development from going very far.

Yes, I have some work for you.

We have several research outposts in various w-space systems. It's common, one of those things that nobody discusses but everybody knows about anyway. A while ago, they recovered bits of ancient technology which seemed to have unusual properties.. We thought for a while it might be some sort of Sleeper computer core, but now it appears to be Talocan in origin. Another of our laboratories has more pieces, and they're suggesting it's actually the core of a station's life-support system, with multiple redundant modules that can back each other up and be easily replaced if they fail. They're setting up to test their theory right now at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I need you to take our samples over so they can complete the network they've pieced together.

That is very good to hear, thank you. We will transfer the cargo to your hangar immediately, along with a small element of the intelligence team, who have stated that they will provide security through to the final destination station. You'd best head to your ship quickly, as I wouldn't want those guys on board my ship without an escort, especially as the rather unique weapons they usually carry are easily capable of punching a nice little hole in your hull.

As you probably know all too well, speed is the lifeblood of the Republic's defense fleets, particularly for the smaller frigates and cruisers. There's a lot that goes into it: low-density reactor cores, kinesthetic maneuvering thrusters, hyper-responsive gyroscopic stabilizers. All the housings are built using nano-alloy rather than the more heavyweight materials the other empires use; it was simply more convenient back when the ships were first designed, but it gives them that little bit of extra boost that's become our signature.

Our R&D specialists have been working on a new formula for the C-86 thermal epoxy resin used on engine housings and other parts of the propulsion systems; I want you to take this batch over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for application and field testing.

Our R&D specialists have been working on a more efficient design for the inertial compensators which keep the drive components from shaking themselves to bits; I want you to take this batch over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for application and field testing.

See, I told you this would be a smooth run. Customs and the police have been advised that you will be transiting their space and that you are not to be disturbed. Have a safe flight. Hell, you can practically autopilot this one!

Thank you for agreeing to help us. We will have the quantrium moved into your item hangar as soon as possible. You have already been cleared for emergency departure.

We recently found a number of new mining fields in adjacent systems, and the usual assortment of pirate trash has come out of the woodwork to exploit it. We'll need them mined soon because even those thieving bastards have friends in places high enough to put the legal status of these sites in doubt. For some reason they've taken an interest even in Banidine, too, and we'll need to find out why; all my workers are busy with the more profitable fields, but I'm not taking any chances.

I'm uploading a bookmark to your People & Places databank; it shows the location of a Banidine mining operation. I need you to head out there and mine all the Banidine. Should be 18,000 units, my foreman tells me. Once we've made an undisputed claim, we're free to mine there again without interference, and I'll provide you with a little something for your trouble.

My boss wants Banidine; something to do with manufacturing cheaper parts for refrigeration units or something. I don't know. Point is, he's made it my job to get the ore. And now I'm makin' it your job.

There's a few Banidine rocks out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enough for 20,000 units, the scouts tell me. Go out there, mine it, bring it back. Should be easy enough, right?

We've gotten word of the location of a bunch of Mercium ore here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but we believe that our information has also been leaked to other factions, including the Gallenteans. It's vital that you collect all the Mercium: It cannot be allowed to fall into enemy hands.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

We've found an old mining post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But, the thing is, we can't find who used to own it: There are no records of its being built or even existing. It's simply empty. No sign of anyone left there, dead or otherwise. Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks; you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Anyway, near as we can tell, the miners were working on a large Lyavite deposit. They didn't finish, because there's still about 5,000 units of it at the site. Now, I know Lyavite isn't the most popular rock, but nobody just leaves that much ore lying around. And besides, the brains at the lab figure they can use the stuff for some of their research, so this opportunity is too good to pass up.

That's where you come in. Warp in, mine the Lyavite, and warp out. It's that easy.

Well, we've located some asteroids that contain substantial amounts of Polygypsum. It's a comparatively rare mineral, and almost completely unknown in this system. Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with the stuff. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. So what do you think? Are you in?

Polygypsum is widely considered worthless because of the dangers associated with storing and reprocessing it. As a result, you won't find this ore on the market. In fact, for this reason, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it as a unique entry in the computers when they install standard ship scanners.

If you're having trouble finding the correct ore at the mission location, you can right-click the "Polygypsum" icon in the mission details in your Opportunities interface and select "Add to Overview."

A short time ago, Minmatar terrorists in a combined fleet of frigates and cruisers attacked one of our Harbinger-class battlecruisers as it was transporting slaves from a recently closed mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in a nearby system. While all but one of the attackers was annihilated, our convoy's escorts were destroyed and our cruiser is burning. Making a bad situation worse, we are anticipating that the terrorists will return in force within the next several hours to attempt the theft of our slaves, as they almost certainly know the cruiser is alone and all but helpless.

Our concern is that if the terrorists feel that they have a window of opportunity to recover these slaves, it is likely that they will throw everything they have into the effort. Our intelligence assessments of the terrorists' fleet assets are even less reassuring: we believe that they could send as many as four battlecruisers into this fight – more than enough to wipe out the arriving frigates and forcefully board our heavily damaged strategic cruiser. However, we have calculated that if we can delay any terrorist boarding parties long enough, this should give us enough time for the much larger main rescue fleet to arrive.

The only bright side to this situation, in what is unquestionably an act of divine providence, is that a large contingent of marines are aboard this station as we speak, having just completed specialized refresher training in counter-boarding operations. We need you to deliver them to the station closest to the last reported position of our cruiser. From there, we will transport a combined team of marines, engineers, medics, and other essential personnel to hopefully stop the fire and save the ship - along with its cargo of highly valuable slaves. However, this mission must be undertaken immediately. Any delay will surely doom the Harbinger and her brave crew.

While transporting Minmatar slaves from a recently close ore mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in nearby system, the convoy was attacked by terrorists, destroying the escort frigates and heavily damaging the Harbinger-class battlecruiser carrying the slaves. We believe it is likely that the terrorists will return, and in larger ships, to attempt a rescue of the slaves before we can respond with reinforcements. The window of opportunity for the terrorists is short, so it is imperative that we immediately render as much help as possible. What we need you to do is deliver a contingent of heavily armed marines recently trained in counter-boarding operations to a station closer to the site of the battle. From there, they will join other Amarr military and rescue teams for immediate transportation to the damaged cruiser.

{[character]player.name}! Glad you could make it on such short notice. Let me get right to the point: Yesterday, as you almost certainly know, a regional governor delivered her State of the Region address. Needless to say, we were quite excited and thus put forth a maximum effort to ensure that her speech was broadcast on every possible channel and to the maximum ranges of our civilian and military communications networks.

However, for various reasons at many remote locations, this signal did not reach many who would have otherwise benefitted from this opportunity. For all our efforts, there are some locations that can only be reached the hard way -- ferrying holoreels directly to each and every one of them. We have already dispatched messengers, primarily in interceptors and other fast ships, to these more dangerous destinations.

We need you to transport a quantity of holoreels containing the State of the Region speech to one station in particular and hand them over to an agent who will be waiting for them there. He will then handle all further distribution of the 'reels.

So, can you help us with what should be a straightforward courier job?

The regional governor herself delivered an important State of the Region speech yesterday to all her billions of faithful followers. Due to technical problems, however, this message did not reach as many citizens as it should have. Fortunately, we have managed to correct this rather quickly through dispatching a small fleet of interceptors to the problem locations. We need you, however, to take a shipment of holoreels to the station we designate, as our usual contact there is indisposed at the moment and may not be available for some time. When you deliver these to that station, our contact's second-in-command will take charge of the cargo and facilitate further broadcasting.
Thank you so very much, {[character]player.name}. The Amarr representative has already informed us that he is offloading the holoreels as we speak. We will not forget this service to the Empire.

I must say we are quite disappointed. As you know, all of our pilots are gone, taking these 'reels to the faithful. Your refusal leaves a gap in this coverage that will leave many faithful Amarr without this important message from the governor.

We've decided to do our agents in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} a favor. They've been complaining for quite some time of being overworked and underpaid, so we've decided to send them the perfect gift to soothe their nerves. A few packs of tobacco should do the trick, heh heh. It's at least something, until we come up with a better solution.

Deliver the batch to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and a local supplier will pick it up from there and deliver it to where they're staying.

A few packs of tobacco should do the trick, heh heh. It's at least something, until we come up with a better solution.

It's tough to quit smoking when you've got a warehouse full of cigarettes within arm's reach. Take every crate of that crap you can find in that warehouse over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and leave it there. Quickly, before I change my mind!

I have assets at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} that are in need of additional protection. We've hired a group of marines to take care of the problem. Go to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off.

I have assets at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} that are in need of additional protection. We've hired a group of marines to take care of the problem. Go to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off.

Colonists eking out a living on godforsaken rocks in space are finding it hard to maintain food production, so we're giving them a boost. The moment you've brought those crates of frozen plant seeds over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, our caravans will pick them up and haul them to those thankful pioneers.

You capsuleers spend so much time in the midst of mayhem and destruction, and you leave countless wreckages in your wake. Now, though, you and I have an opportunity to help sustain new life. I want you to transport some large crates of frozen plant seeds for me.

It will not surprise you that we are always trying to establish new colonies in even the most desolate parts of space. Colonization is always an exciting opportunity, not only for the settlers who dare venture out into space and stake their fortunes on some desolate rock, but for local entrepreneurs, businesses and politicians to support them. You won't hear of these, because your kind is so far up above piddly little local events, but it's a big deal for those involved.

Unfortunately, local support can't last forever. After the initial interest has waned, the citizens on those colonies have to fend for themselves. Sometimes they manage to create self-sustaining habitats where no outside intervention is needed. Occasionally they get lucky, and the outcome of their scientific experiments, ore search, or whatever else they were up to, makes them enough money that they can buy whatever they need off local orbitals.

All too often, though, we have to step in. Your cargo, once delivered to their colony, will hopefully enable them to bootstrap themselves to a self-sustaining life cycle. Colony life is hard enough as it is.
Really? Ah well, back to destruction it is.
I am greatly disappointed. Their food stores were already running low.
Take care to keep those seeds frozen at all times.
Excellent. Caravans will take the seeds to the colony. You have earned back some of your karma, capsuleer.

Some entertainment-hungry collectors out there are waiting for a lot of specially ordered holoreels that were manufactured, stamped, signed and compiled in special editions elsewhere in the cluster. I need you to bring these large holoreel crates to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} before they risk starting something silly like reading books.

Most often we leave the shipment of entertainment material to the more slow-moving vessels in our employ. Every so often, though, we receive sufficient premium orders from other stations and the planets in their vicinity that we dispatch a special courier with the payload.

That courier is you, and the payload is huge stacks of holoreels, most of them ordered on some manner of timed interstellar delivery offer.

This isn't the primary business of our own corporation as such, but we have enough ties to the producers of all this material - as would any corporation large enough to have gone interstellar - that it's incumbent on us to find ways of delivering it to the customers.

Believe me, I wish we could just transfer all of this digitally, but for most of this cargo that is simply not an option. Some of these holoreels are under trade restrictions that prevent them from being beamed over and saved or stamped on the spot; others are special collectors' editions that may include anything from specially signed copies to boxed sets weighed down with any number of collectable objects.

Please ensure your crew doesn't open any of the crates, either. These people are collectors and paid a galactic premium for their items. If they so much as smell another human being's presence on the merchandise, they will resort either to lawsuits or assassinations.
Very well. They'll just have to watch empty screens for a little longer.
The customers will not be happy with this.
Don't open any of those sealed special editions, you hear?
Excellent. Your crew left the holoreels untouched, I trust.

We have come into possession of large amounts of garbage, and since we can't legally rid ourselves of it here, I need you to transport it over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. They have some good people there who don't have ethical qualms about destroying any kind of trash, even if a limb or two is dangling out of the crate.

In all honesty, I find it just unbelievable that in this day and age we are expending actual capsuleer man-hours, not to mention the time and effort of your crew, and asking actual spaceships to travel interstellar distances only to shift around a cargohold of something as pitiable as actual garbage. Garbage. Especially the type we've got here, which takes up a bunch of room, has to be stored in nonporous containers, and, frankly, is starting to smell.

Nonetheless, here we are. We could have this cargo sent down planetside and destroyed, except that while those people are perfectly happy to toss up any number of shipments with whatever trinkets the station clientele is demanding that week, they have frothing conniptions if we so much as suggest that we might want to send anything like this back down in return. The merest whisper of it is enough for them to drag out the lawyers. It's not as if they don't have the space.

You aren't too big to help out, I trust. All we need you to do is haul this smelly, half-liquidized garbage to another station, where they'll have ways to get rid of it without endless complaints or moral qualms. I swear, if the PR department would just let us stop accepting all these colony refugees, we wouldn't have this problem.

Actually, forget I said that last part.
Look, it was just normal, everyday garbage. There was no reason for you not to take this on.
I am disappointed. I hope you didn't root around in the cargo.
If your crew tells you that anything was moving in the garbage, don't believe them.
Thanks. Now we have them off our hands. The garbage, I mean.  Off our hands.

We have a small outburst of violent behavior to deal with on a nearby station. Refugees from interstellar violence have begun gathering forces and are demanding compensation, hearings and whatnot. Now, this is just a damn stupid situation, and we have people who can put it right, but they need a bit of a boost. That's where you come in. Transport these large crates of small arms to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll take it from there.

Our people at a nearby station are in need of more firepower. They are going to have to subdue unruly refugees from destroyed colonies and crews from recently destroyed ships.

I know it sounds ludicrous. The thing is, when you have near-death experiences of that kind, you may come to the realization that life is fickle, short and dangerous, and that everything you took for granted may be taken from you in the blink of an eye. It tends to upset people, make them aggressive and reckless.

That is, if they're mortal. You being a capsuleer, you'll just have to take my word for it. I'm sure death has a great impact on your sense of the world, but thus far in my experience, it doesn't make you half as crazy as near-death, and at least your type has the sense to take it outside when you feel the need to blow something up.

Incidentally, there are always claims - by silly local news outlets nobody listens to - that representatives of our corporation may not always react immediately when they hear that people are floating out there in escape pods, waiting in to be rescued. Do not let those claims bother you. Those same people are sitting in the midst of a deadly capsuleer battlefield and are in dire need of learning the blessed virtue of patience.
Alright. We'll have to find other ways of subduing them, then.
I'm disappointed. I hope you're not siding with these rebellious people.
I know you have plenty of firepower, too, but let's leave this one to station personnel.
Thanks! And don't feel bad for those people - I'm sure there'll be some survivors.

You have a juicy and slightly sticky mission on your hands. Quafe is conducting one of their local marketing campaigns and are in need of exotic drinks - which in this case means another shipment of Quafe manufactured in another solar system. Bring these large crates of quafe over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and you'll make a lot of thirsty people very happy.

Quafe is preparing for one of their routine planetside campaigns, and as a premium they want to offer special bottles of the ubiquitous drink.

To be honest, there is nothing special about the drink. It's the same cola, with the same water, color, sugar, additives and perfectly legal trace elements, that you'd find on any civilized planet in the cluster. What's important isn't so much the brand as the bottles themselves . They were manufactured on another planet, so their design is subtly different from what's available where you're taking them, and the labeling indicates their origins.

People go crazy for this stuff. I'm serious. This will be hard for a capsuleer to understand, but most people don't even travel that much between the continents on their own planets. To hold in your hand an item that was manufactured in another solar system is an experience that's truly special to a huge number of people.

This only works for things like Quafe, mind you. Taking anything this thoroughly familiar and changing it just slightly has a higher excitement freakout value than even if you'd brought in some unknown artifact made by actual aliens.
You sure? But everybody loves Quafe!
That's a disappointment. If you and your crew drank it all, it's okay to say so. You're not the only ones with a habit.
Keep moving. I don't trust the sealants on those crates, and I'd hate for the Quafe to go flat.
Perfect. Help yourself to a nice, cool, fizzy drink as a reward.

Our pod fluid vats in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are in dire need of refilling, lest you find yourself floating in something that's more like a swamp lake after a hot summer. Collect from your hangar those large crates of ectoplasm we dredged up and haul them over there as soon as you can!

You capsuleers are amazing. Not only have you got the interstellar corporations doing crazy business in ore, minerals, modules and ammunition, but you also routinely exhaust our storages for the equipment that's required to even keep you people in the air. I need you to transport something that's vital for your own continued success.

I'm not referring to the capsules themselves or the unimaginably complex electronics that help you interface with your ship. No, this is something much more mundane. We need to replenish our vats of pod fluid, and for that, we need ectoplasm. This way, whenever you visit our fair station, we can drain and replace your capsule if our tests show that its contents have become a little too stale.

Also, should you have a clone contract with any of our stations and later on find yourself inconvenienced to the point of ... well, to the point of death, we want to ensure that we can put you into a new capsule filled to the brim with pod fluid that's proper, fresh and new. Nothing's quite as disgusting as waking up in a brand new body only to realize that it's been plunged into someone else's used pod fluid.
Fair enough. Keep floating in your own goo, then.
Really? Alright, but don't be surprised if your pod starts to thicken up a little in time.
You'll ... not want to taste the cargo. Trust me.
Wonderful. We'll happily let you try out the first batch.

I'm not going to beat around the bush with you on this one, as there isn't any time. We have a developing emergency in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name}. Several of our commercial convoys have been ripped to shreds in the last few months by an extremely dangerous band of terrorists. As you can see from these camera drone recordings, they have even been willing to fly their ships directly into our freighters and other unarmed haulers. And yes, before you ask, we have been escorting these convoys with heavily armed security vessels, though to little effect.

As these terrorists are obviously willing to die for their cause, they aren't bothering to attack our warships. They simply seem to appear out of nowhere, accelerate to high speeds and slam into the cargo ships. Depending on the cargo, this action can, at best, tear open the cargo bays and release the contents into the vacuum of space, or, at worst, strike a shipment of fuels or ammunition, and destroy the freighter in one huge explosion. One such explosion destroyed an entire convoy.

However, an ultra-secure communications intercept satellite recently picked up a communication that we believe indicates the terrorists are now considering turning their deadly tactic against some unidentified stations in the region. Given our huge civilian population on these stations, the decision has been made to conduct a partial evacuation of all potential target stations.

What we need from you is your help in getting these civilians – mostly the spouses and children of station personnel – to a station that is further away from the terrorists' known area of operation. Normally, I would not ask this of a capsuleer, but I am begging you: will you help us evacuate these people until this threat has passed? We need to know right now, as we have already begun to organize the evacuation fleet; can we count you in?

He'll get into heaps of trouble with his superiors if they find out, so I want you to help him make the problem go away. Fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop off a new set of weapons. I'll modify the ID codes on the guns, and nobody will suspect a thing.

One of our R&D facilities has been working hard to produce a new type of cloaking device for Covert Ops vessels that will allow those ships to remain cloaked while jumping stargates. However, it has recently been brought to our attention that a corporate espionage agent sent by a rival company is targeting this new technology, for obvious reasons. In order to flush him out and arrest him, however, we need to catch him in the act. So, we are asking you to transport a decoy prototype cloaking device from this station to one we designate. With such a juicy target, we feel the spy will not be able to resist making an attempt to steal it somewhere between here and there. We need you to fly this device to that station utilizing absolute secrecy.

Surprisingly, people seem to enjoy visiting {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}. I personally think the place is rather boring, but command has ordered me to take care of some high-profile tourists for the next week. Ferry these tourists over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me, would you? That should keep them busy, at least.
